title: A Sub-Aperture-Based Ray-Tracing Framework for Near-Field U-MIMO THz Communications
summary: Terahertz (THz) communications are characterized by antennas with large apertures and extended near-field (NF) region, offering the opportunity to develop adaptable beam manipulation strategies, particularly related to ultra-massive MIMO (U-MIMO). While Ray-Tracing (RT) offers an attractive alternative to full-wave methods, conventional ray-based approaches are generally formulated under far-field (FF) assumptions. We propose a technique that extends RT to the NF regime, enabling ray-based NF characterization of transmitting arrays. We model the transmitting array as an antenna aperture and develop a RT framework that partitions the transmitting aperture into sub-apertures emitting FF contributions which can be propagated via geometric optics (GO). We develop a Ray-Launching algorithm based on the proposed framework and assess its beam-reconstruction accuracy against full-wave propagation. The results demonstrate that, through tunable aperture partitioning, the proposed approach can reproduce beam manipulation effects characteristic of NF U-MIMO THz communications using GO ray propagation.
authors: Federico Ruggeri; Sotiris Droulias; Jiming Chen; Angeliki Alexiou; Jie Zhang

title: Structured Pruning of Feedback Delay Networks
summary: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) are recursive filter structures used to synthesise artificial reverberation. Their feedback matrix governs both energy exchange between delay lines and the computation required at every sample, making its design central to balancing an FDN's acoustic performance and implementation efficiency. In this work, we develop an FDN-specific structured pruning method that connects these acoustic and computational concerns, allowing high-order dense orthogonal designs to be fitted to efficient implementations. The feedback matrix is replaced by stages of fixed permutations and small orthogonal blocks. We characterise connectivity growth with the network depth and derive exact conditional block updates for matrix fitting, followed by refinement against the reference FDN magnitude response. The resulting factors admit direct vectorised evaluation, with arithmetic cost and coefficient storage scaling linearly with network size for fixed block size and depth. On an Apple M2, the selected staged kernels achieve feedback-multiplication speedups over dense BLAS ranging from approximately threefold to over twentyfold across the tested network sizes, while substantially reducing coefficient storage. Objective metrics and listening tests indicate that the proposed staged approximations closely preserve the spectral and temporal character of their dense references. An analysis of processor utilisation and register reuse explains why execution time depends on more than the operation count. Finally, block size and depth provide practical control over response fidelity, storage, and real-time cost, allowing acoustic design to precede the choice of an efficient implementation.
authors: Facundo Franchino; Karolina Prawda

title: Channel State Information-Free Angle Spoofing for Differential Localization Privacy
summary: This paper proposes a channel state information (CSI)-free angle spoofing strategy that remains effective even when the eavesdropper (Eve) uses differential statistics to estimate the location of the transmitter (Alice). Specifically, by designing a precoding matrix, Eve incorrectly estimates the angle differences of departure (ADoDs), thereby spoofing Alice's location. Meanwhile, the trusted user (Bob) can still infer Alice's true location with a modest amount of securely shared side information. Given the channel parameters estimated by Eve from the spoofed channel, the resulting localization bias introduced to the eavesdroppers under the spoofed geometric is analyzed. Eve's bias can be driven to infinity asymptotically in a key parameter of the precoder. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method introduces significant localization errors for Eve. When combined with a prior CSI-free spoofing strategy, further degraded performance is achieved by Eve.
authors: Lei Lyu; Urbashi Mitra

title: Streaming Speech Recognition on a Microcontroller: a 65.7M-Parameter Transducer in 2 and 4 Bits on the ESP32-P4
summary: We run Kroko, a 65.7M-parameter streaming Zipformer2 transducer for English, on the ESP32-P4, a microcontroller with two 400 MHz RISC-V cores, a 128-bit SIMD extension (PIE) and 32 MB of PSRAM, but no neural accelerator. Without any training, the encoder's 290 matrices are stored with 2 or 4 bits per weight in Hadamard-rotated groups: the width of each matrix comes from its measured sensitivity, and each matrix is first corrected toward the original model's output, then rounded with GPTQ and a search over the group norms. The released 71 MB of int8 weights become a 26.65 MB file. Activations are int16 between the matrix products and int8 into them. A C engine with hand-written PIE kernels processes each 1.28 s chunk of audio in 0.90 s on both cores, beam search included, and its PC build computes the same bits as the chip, so accuracy is measured on whole test sets. LibriSpeech WER is 4.34% on test-clean and 10.26% on test-other, against 3.94% and 9.17% for the released model; on FLEURS and Common Voice the gap grows to 2.3 and 1.1 points. A GPU simulator shows that the integer arithmetic costs nothing and that the whole gap comes from the weights, and an ablation on all of test-clean shows that GPTQ does most of the work. We also report the port's speed history, from 51.3 s to 0.62 s of encoder time per chunk, each design step measured again in one build, an attempt to reach 16 MB that stopped at 19.63 MB, and what did not work. We did not measure energy. The inference engine, the firmware and the 2/4-bit weights are available at https://github.com/BoumedineBillal/esp32-pie-asr.
authors: Billal Boumedine

title: Personalising Parametric Audio Effect Recommendation for Vocals from Parameter-only Style Priors
summary: Audio effect recommendation has mostly modelled style through reference audio and audio-domain losses. Because the parameter-to-audio map of parametric effects is many-to-one, such systems can match a reference without reflecting how a given engineer works. We instead model an engineer's style as a distribution over effect-chain parameters, which matches the data engineers can realistically share: console recalls store parameters without the audio they were applied to. Under a label-shift assumption, a personalised recommendation follows in closed form from a generic content model, a parameter population model and an engineer prior, with no paired engineer audio and no tuned weights. For vocal chains, the content signal is small but real, and concentrated in high-frequency EQ, dynamics and reverb. A forced-choice test with $14$ listeners found that the style-prior and content-only recommendations were distinguishable (89.3%), with results consistent with prior width affecting the balance between style and content, while parameter-space cosine does not predict perceived difference.
authors: Soumya Sai Vanka; Hayato Yamakawa; Kazunobu Kondo; Yu Takahashi; György Fazekas

title: Minimum-Time Trajectory for Escort-Assisted Evasion from a Sensing-Limited Pursuer
summary: This paper studies a minimum-time path-planning problem in which an escort assists a leader by triggering and redirecting a sensing-limited pursuer. For the post-engagement case with equal leader, escort, and pursuer speeds, we show that the minimum-time leader trajectory has a three-phase structure: an initial straight segment, a moving-boundary segment, and a final straight segment to the goal. The boundary-following kinematics and the corresponding entry and exit conditions are derived and used to construct the leader trajectory for a fixed escort engagement direction. The engagement direction is then optimized over the feasible set to obtain the minimum-time solution. Numerical results illustrate the resulting trajectory and the benefits of escort assistance.
authors: Al Faysal; Alexander Von Moll; Artur Wolek; Satyanarayana G. Manyam; Thomas Chapman; Isaac Weintraub; David Casbeer; Dipankar Maity

title: Wav2Aug: A Drop-In Speech Augmentation Policy
summary: SpecAugment is the dominant speech augmentation policy, but researchers have studied it primarily for automatic speech recognition (ASR), and it operates on spectrograms, limiting its applicability to other speech tasks and waveform models. We propose Wav2Aug, a drop-in waveform augmentation policy that randomly samples two augmentations from a calibrated pool of waveform transformations. We calibrate the augmentation hyperparameters once and reuse them across tasks and architectures, eliminating task-specific tuning. Experiments on ten speech benchmarks show that Wav2Aug achieves ASR performance comparable to SpecAugment while improving over it on average across non-ASR tasks, yielding an average relative error reduction of 12.8% over the strongest compatible SpecAugment baseline. We further show that multi-view training provides additional gains, with two augmented views offering the best tradeoff between performance and computational cost.
authors: Gianfranco Dumoulin Bertucci; Mirco Ravanelli

title: Finite-State Uncertainty-Aware Widely-Linear Equalization for Aeronautical GMSK Links
summary: Aeronautical and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receivers must equalize doubly selective channels under synchronization uncertainty and limited onboard computation and memory. We propose a finite-state, uncertainty-aware widely-linear (WL) equalization algorithm for Gaussian minimum-shift keying (GMSK) links. The algorithm uses synchronization estimates and their reliability descriptors to select one of a small number of precomputed filters, avoiding repeated online coefficient synthesis. Using a finite-memory Laurent model, we design the stored affine WL filters from conditional physical-state moments. We derive an exact characterization of excess mean-square error (MSE) relative to adaptation to continuous side information, Lloyd-type conditions for finite-state design, local timing--frequency mismatch certificates, and an orthogonal decomposition of design and information losses. On a reference channel at $E_b/N_0=8$~dB under high synchronization-estimation uncertainty, a $16$-state bank reduces pseudo-symbol MSE by $51.9\%$ relative to point-estimate WL time-varying MMSE equalization and by $6.6\%$ relative to posterior-mean (PM) substitution. With identical partitioning, routing, and storage, conditional-moment filters reduce MSE by $10.1\%$ and full-waveform average bit error rate (ABER) by $15.6\%$ relative to representative-state filters. Across $18$ synthetic three-path channels with individually fitted banks, MSE and ABER decrease by $5.3\%$ and $12.9\%$, respectively, relative to PM substitution. The $16$-state receiver stores $2048$ real coefficients. Posterior integration, robustness sweeps, and software timing measurements quantify the tradeoff between equalization accuracy, online computational cost, and bank refresh.
authors: Ahmad Tanha; Ali Khalesi

title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation
summary: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feature distillation with text and click conditioning, and then fine-tune the separator using the adapted visual features. We also introduce an on-screen interference setting, where both the target and interferer are visible, to evaluate target selectivity. Experiments on standard benchmarks and the on-screen interference setting demonstrate consistent improvements in separation quality and target selectivity, particularly for mixtures containing semantically similar sources.
authors: Suyeon Lee; Doyeop Kwak; Joon Son Chung

title: MiDiff: MIDI-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Drum Audio Enhancement
summary: Bridging the semantic gap between perfect symbolic musical structure and severely degraded acoustic signals offers a powerful paradigm for high-fidelity audio restoration. We introduce MiDiff, a diffusion-based generative model for drum audio enhancement that conditions the reverse process on temporally aligned Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) piano rolls. We extend the Score-Based Generative Models for Speech Enhancement (SGMSE) framework in the complex Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) domain by integrating a pretrained MIDI encoder, multi-scale temporal alignment, and three complementary conditioning strategies: early injection, Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), and cross-attention. We further show that providing the same piano roll only through classifier guidance, driven by an Automatic Drum Transcription (ADT) model on the audio-only score, yields no measurable gain: the symbolic prior is effective when it conditions the score network. To relax the requirement for ground-truth MIDI at inference, we further propose a hybrid reverse schedule that transcribes the diffusion state online with the same noise-aware ADT network and hands over from the audio-only score to MiDiff at a tunable switch time, cutting test FAD by 47% relative to the audio-only baseline without any symbolic input (switch time selected on the test set). We train our model on the StemGMD dataset using a non-additive degradation pipeline that simulates room reverberation with echo, electret capsule frequency response, and soft-clipping saturation with noise. MiDiff substantially outperforms the SGMSE baseline in terms of Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) on both the validation and held-out test sets. Ablation studies demonstrate that combining all three conditioning strategies yields superior performance and that authentic MIDI velocity dynamics are critical for effective symbolic conditioning.
authors: Elad Aspis; Sharon Gannot

title: From the Superderivative to a Relative-Gradient Edge Operator
summary: First-derivative edge detectors such as Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts and Scharr measure absolute grey-level differences. We revisit the log-gradient magnitude, a relative-gradient edge operator, and motivate it by analogy with the superderivative, a multiplicative derivative in which the independent variable is perturbed multiplicatively rather than additively. In one and two dimensions the logarithm of the superderivative is a radial logarithmic derivative; its local, origin-free, isotropic analogue is the magnitude of the logarithmic gradient. The resulting operator measures relative rather than absolute change, giving an edge-strength map that is invariant under global intensity rescaling. We present the theory, show how the operator can be implemented in two steps---a classical gradient kernel plus a pointwise division---and compare it with standard first-derivative filters on synthetic images with ground-truth edges and on the official BSDS500 benchmark. We also study a parametric family that interpolates between the absolute gradient and the log-gradient; empirically, the best members are small intermediate exponents, which edge the classical kernels by a small but statistically detectable margin in the per-image metric and, with the same Gaussian smoothing as the single-$σ$ Canny, match it in ODS and lead it in OIS and AP, while the tuned Canny remains ahead in ODS. The single-threshold margin over the kernels does not replicate on the held-out test split, and the fully relative endpoint is never the best member, its ranking depending on the edge-map normalisation. The contribution is the construction and the invariance it buys, not a new state of the art.
authors: Alejandro Garnung Menéndez

title: pCoRev: Physics-Informed Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Reverberation Artifact Suppression in Ultrafast Plane-Wave Imaging
summary: Reverberation artifact suppression in ultrafast plane-wave (PW) imaging remains challenging because artifact-free reference data are generally unavailable and multipath echoes often resemble tissue signals. Coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC) attenuates reverberation only partially and sacrifices the frame rate that motivates PW imaging. We propose pCoRev, an unsupervised physics-informed contrastive learning framework that leverages the distinct angular coherence characteristics of tissue echoes and reverberation artifacts. A single-angle I/Q frame is the network input, and the remaining angles of the same CPWC acquisition provide angle-consistent positive pairs, residual-derived negative pairs, and coherence-guided self-supervision, so no paired artifact-free data are required. On a fabricated reverberation phantom with 31 validation acquisitions, pCoRev achieved the best contrast ratio (CR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and generalized CNR (gCNR) of 38.76 +/- 5.40 dB, 11.75 +/- 1.81 dB, and 0.932 +/- 0.051 against delay-and-sum (DAS), delay-multiply-and-sum, a supervised 3D convolutional neural network, and unsupervised deep coherence learning. Because the network is trained on single-angle inputs, it also operates on a single PW transmission: with one angle, pCoRev reached a CR of 32.10 +/- 7.79 dB and a CNR of 10.39 +/- 3.02 dB, exceeding 75-angle compounded DAS (20.45 +/- 3.84 dB and 8.38 +/- 2.00 dB) with 75-fold fewer transmissions. On four clinical acquisitions from other scanners, pCoRev improved CR over DAS by 9 to 21 dB without fine-tuning. These results indicate that physics-informed unsupervised contrastive learning suppresses reverberation effectively while preserving the frame-rate advantage of ultrafast PW imaging.
authors: Hyunwoo Cho; Yeeun Kwon; Yangmo Yoo; Jinbum Kang

title: A Parallel Two-Stage Prony Framework for Robust Delay-Doppler Estimation
summary: This paper addresses off-grid physical delay-Doppler parameter estimation based on an orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) pilot waveform over doubly selective channels. Based on a known single-pilot waveform with a frequency-shifted sinc pulse structure, we propose a parallel dual-order estimation framework, in which Prony-based Doppler-first and delay-first procedures are executed concurrently and their candidate paths are jointly fused. The two estimation orders provide complementary resolution characteristics, thereby mitigating ambiguities caused by closely spaced multipath components and fractional delay--Doppler mismatch. Numerical results show that the proposed framework improves detection reliability and estimation stability compared with a single-order Prony estimator, especially in off-grid scenarios and low-to-moderate signal-to-noise ratio regimes.
authors: Liangchen Sun; Yutaka Jitsumatsu

title: Movable Beyond-Diagonal RIS for ISAC: Optimal Placement and Pareto Boundary
summary: This letter investigates integrated sensing and communication using a movable beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS). Under a rank-one line-of-sight BS--RIS channel, we derive the exact communication--sensing Pareto boundary of a fully-connected BD-RIS in terms of user--target channel correlation. For line-of-sight RIS links, maximizing this correlation yields the optimal placement. We characterize the minimum track aperture that eliminates the illumination trade-off and show that a movable diagonal RIS then attains the same optimum. Below this threshold, a dynamic program offers certified placement accuracy. Numerical results examine hardware connectivity, angular mismatch, and Rician fading.
authors: Chandan Kumar Sheemar; Sourabh Solanki; Symeon Chatzinotas

title: Weak and Strong Data Informativity with Structural Priors for System Analysis
summary: When measurement data are insufficient for unique system identification, data informativity evaluates whether a dataset determines a property across all systems consistent with the data. This paper introduces a unified framework distinguishing between weak and strong data informativity under prior structural knowledge described by affine constraints: data are weakly informative if at least one system consistent with the data and prior knowledge possesses the target property, and strongly informative if every consistent system satisfies it. The latter is consistent with the notion of data informativity in the existing literature. By explicitly parameterizing all consistent systems as affine functions of free parameters via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we characterize these notions for fundamental system properties-including controllability, stabilizability, and stability. This formulation establishes that verifying weak and strong informativity, when tractable, reduces to rank tests of matrix pencils constructed from the data and prior knowledge. Our findings show that structural priors can lower data-excitation requirements and enable reliable analysis even when data fail to be strongly informative. Finally, the framework is extended to a class of noisy data.
authors: Yuan Zhang; Wenxuan Xu; Yun Feng; Keke Huang; Keyou You

title: Phase-Compensated Frequency-Scan Measurement of Harmonic Transfer Function Impedance
summary: Impedance models obtained through frequency scanning provides terminal characterization for small-signal stability analysis without requiring detailed knowledge of internal converter parameters. When unbalanced steady-state components introduce cross-frequency coupling, conventional $2\times2$ impedance scan methods must be extended to identify harmonic transfer function (HTF) impedance. However, the measured phases of frequency-coupling terms depend on the starting time of the fast Fourier transform (FFT) window, potentially introducing phase errors when different time references are used. This paper presents a $dq$-domain measurement method of HTF impedance that explicitly accounts for this time dependence. Phase compensation aligns the measured Fourier coefficients to a common electrical phase reference, correcting the resulting phase discrepancies and enabling consistent impedance reconstruction. Comparisons with analytical models under balanced and unbalanced conditions verify the measurement method, recovering the conventional $2\times2$ impedance and the dominant coupling blocks of a $6\times6$ HTF representation, respectively.
authors: Yiyang Liao; Yitong Li; Jinjun Liu

title: Beyond Fresnel Approximation: Exact Airy Beamforming for Near-Field THz Communications
summary: Line-of-sight (LoS) blockage can severely degrade the performance of conventional focused beams in terahertz (THz) communications. Recently, bending beams (e.g., Airy beams) have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to bypass obstacles by propagating along curved trajectories under near-field propagation conditions. However, existing Airy-beam designs in wireless communications often rely on the Fresnel approximation for the focal distance, which becomes inaccurate at large steering angles or short propagation distances. To address this limitation, this letter proposes a more accurate Airy beamforming design method based on the exact focal-distance expression and the corresponding caustic geometry. Specifically, we jointly optimize the bending curvature, virtual focal distance, and steering angle to maximize the received signal power subject to receiver-alignment and obstacle-avoidance constraints. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem, we first use geometric preprocessing to narrow the feasible range of the bending curvature. Then, a two-layer optimization framework is developed with the outer and inner layers optimizing the bending curvature and the other two parameters, respectively. Numerical results based on the cascaded geometrical and wave channel model demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher received signal power than conventional Airy-beam designs and offers complementary advantages over conventional focused beams under different blockage ratios.
authors: Fangjie Shen; Weidong Mei; Aoran Liu; Peilan Wang; Zhi Chen

title: Adaptive Orbit-Aided Vector Tracking for Orbit Determination of LEO Satellites
summary: Reliable orbit determination for CubeSats is essential for emerging low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation, and timing (LEO-PNT) applications. However, onboard orbit determination remains constrained by single-frequency GNSS code-based receivers, intermittent signal reception, and highly dynamic orbital conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive orbit-aided vector tracking (OAVT) algorithm for LEO-PNT CubeSat orbit determination under these conditions. The method employs a GNSS vector tracking loop (VTL) as the primary navigation estimator and loosely couples it with a low-fidelity orbital dynamics model (ODM), which provides auxiliary position and velocity pseudo-measurements. The contribution of the ODM is regulated through adaptive covariance assignment based on GNSS stress and the residual consistency between the ODM and GNSS solutions. Under nominal conditions, OAVT preserves the accuracy advantage of VTL over the conventional scalar tracking loop. The 3D position root-mean-square error (RMSE) is reduced from 2.631\,m for STL to 1.081\,m, while the 3D velocity RMSE decreases from 0.3985\,m/s to 0.1023\,m/s. Under degraded conditions, OAVT provides substantially greater robustness than both STL and standalone VTL. The 3D position RMSE remains bounded at 8.27\,m during a complete signal outage, 10.17\,m during gradual signal loss and reacquisition, and 26.65\,m under variable visibility, whereas STL fails to produce valid solutions and standalone VTL loses lock. These results demonstrate that OAVT substantially improves solution robustness and state continuity with only a moderate increase in computational burden, making it suitable for CubeSat orbit determination and future LEO-PNT missions.
authors: Zihong Zhou; Bing Xu

title: Counterfactual Public Opinion Projection for Intervention Decision-Making
summary: Effective public opinion intervention requires forecasts of how the same event would evolve under alternative actions. Existing methods mainly capture observational associations and inadequately address treatment selection bias. The paper proposes a counterfactual public opinion projection framework for intervention decision making. Each intervention is represented by its timing, type, content and intensity. Causal triggering structures are inferred from propagation event sequences. Counterfactual trajectories of attention, sentiment and polarization are generated from adversarially balanced representations. Candidate interventions are then compared through repeated rollouts. Semisynthetic experiments yielded an overall F1 comparable to a direct structure learning baseline and a recall of 0.698 for causal edges linking semantically dissimilar content. Representation diagnostics showed that the gradient reversal layer reduced treatment information leakage from 0.163 to 0.140. Bootstrap analyses of real data further revealed intervention specific model effects on attention, sentiment and polarization.
authors: Ruixing Ren; Junhui Zhao; Qiuping Li; Xiaoke Sun

title: Semantic Anchor Communication System for Point Cloud Transmission in Internet of Vehicles
summary: Joint transmission of point cloud geometry and semantics under bandwidth constraints is required for cooperative perception in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Per-point semantics cannot be explicitly preserved by existing geometric compression methods, while interpretable three-dimensional point sets cannot be directly reconstructed via task-feature communication. The paper proposes a spatial semantic anchor communication system. Distinct from global codewords and task features, anchors with explicit coordinates are employed as transmission units. Local shape descriptors and category labels are bound to a unified spatial reference, preserving the correspondence between local position, shape and semantics. At the transmitter, anchor representations are extracted and then converted into digital frames through fixed-point quantization and lossless compression.Atthereceiver,labeledpoint clouds are reconstructed through anchor-constrained local expansion, and pose-aligned multi-view observations are fused. On the 500-frame SemanticPOSS test set, the results demonstrate that spatial semantic anchors enable interpretable joint reconstruction and fusion of geometry and semantics with low transmission overhead.
authors: Ruixing Ren; Junhui Zhao; Wei Zhao; Gaoxin Zhang; Xiaoming Wang

title: DRC-TTS: A Dual-Resolution Codec-Based Architecture for Lexicon-Free Malay Speech Synthesis
summary: Modern discrete neural audio codecs facilitate speech synthesis by replacing continuous acoustic representations with low-frame-rate discrete token sequences. For Malay speech synthesis, character-level input reduces reliance on pronunciation lexicons. However, combining character-level inputs with low-frame-rate discrete codecs introduces a temporal alignment challenge. When predicted character durations are quantized into frame counts at 12.5 Hz, durations shorter than one codec frame may be assigned zero frames. Consequently, the corresponding character representations may be lost during length regulation, potentially leading to pronunciation omissions. This study proposes DRC-TTS, a dual-resolution codec-based architecture for lexicon-free Malay speech synthesis. The model expands character representations at a temporal resolution of 50 Hz and subsequently downsamples them through strided convolution to 12.5 Hz for discrete codec-token prediction. Objective evaluations show that the proposed model reduces the character error rate (CER) from 27.11% for the baseline to 21.86%, an absolute reduction of 5.25 percentage points. The proposed model also achieves a mean opinion score (MOS) of 4.30, compared with 4.12 for the baseline. These results suggest that the dual-resolution design may improve character-level alignment and perceived speech naturalness under the evaluated conditions.
authors: Tianhui Su; Tien-Ping Tan

title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
summary: AI compute is becoming large and fast-changing electrical loads. Its impacts on data center infrastructure and power grids depend not only on total energy consumption, but also on how their power draw moves over sub-second to minute timescales, including peaks, ramps, and synchronized fluctuations across accelerators. Existing energy benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) report aggregate quantities such as joules per token and rarely release the underlying time-series measurements, leaving these power dynamics poorly characterized and difficult to model. We introduce LLM-PowerTrace, an open dataset of time-resolved, per-GPU power traces for LLM fine-tuning and inference, sampled every 100\,ms on varying NVIDIA platforms paired with complete workload and system metadata. For fine-tuning, LLM-PowerTrace profiles open model families spanning a wide range of model sizes and fine-tuning methods, together with controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing. For inference, it covers variations in concurrency, GPU frequency, KV-cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request-arrival patterns. LLM-PowerTrace profiles a set of open model families across a wide range of model sizes, and controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing for fine-tuning, and it sweeps concurrency, GPU frequency, KV cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request arrival patterns for inference. Built upon power traces, we define power-grid-facing metrics as well as AI-compute power\&energy scaling law for extrapolating beyond the measured settings. Together, LLM-PowerTrace provides a dataset foundation for modeling, forecasting, and managing the fast-changing electrical behavior of AI compute.
authors: Jiansheng Wang; Jaskeerat Singh; Haochen Xu; Xinyi Li; Mingyuan Yan; Shaohui Liu; Yuzhuo Li; Yize Chen; Wenqi Cui

title: Belief-Driven Search in Connectivity-Constrained Mobile Sensor Networks with Convergence Guarantees
summary: Multi-agent search and coverage is critical to autonomous exploration, search-and-rescue, and defense applications. This paper investigates settings where a mobile sensor network is tasked with coordinating to discover the position of a stationary target within a bounded region. We develop a Bayesian update scheme where agents iteratively combine local uncertainties derived from their sensor measurements through inverse variance weighting to get a better global understanding of where the target may be located given some prior belief. Network agents' trajectories are governed by a primal-dual gradient update rule that simultaneously minimizes the expected sensing uncertainty and enforces network connectivity among the agents. We prove that the belief converges to the target under mild, planner-agnostic conditions, with an explicit exponential rate of false-hypothesis rejection and a bound on expected search time. Simulation results show that we can successfully find the target and collapse belief to the ground truth target location while ensuring connectivity of our sensor network. They also empirically confirm our theoretical bounds and revisiting assumption. Finally, we compare against a lawnmower sweep, showing that our method locates the target more quickly when the prior is informative.
authors: George J. Ziavras; Ziqiao Zhang; Shreyas Sundaram; Christopher G. Brinton

title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
summary: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. It introduces neural audio codecs and autoencoders, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization in a shared notation. Worked examples connect training objectives and sampling procedures to published systems. The application sections relate the musical requirements of instrumental generation, songs, editing, and live performance to model design. Comparison tables record representations, methods, inputs, tasks, and release information documented in papers and official sources. Symbolic composition, speech, and sound effects are included where they connect to music audio. We explain how to interpret automatic metrics and learned judges, design and report listening tests, and assess evidence about data provenance, memorization, attribution, and output detection. Selected legal decisions and disputes illustrate the implications for training and release. The reviewed systems combine established generative paradigms with new representations, planning stages, and post-training procedures. Differences in data, scale, and evaluation limit what cross-system comparisons can establish about the sources of reported gains.
authors: Mateusz Modrzejewski; Joanna Kurkowska; Dorien Herremans

title: Necessary and Sufficient Structural Conditions for the Validity of Lyapunov-Type Exponential Stability Criteria
summary: Whether the exponential decay of a Lyapunov function along trajectories implies exponential stability of the state---an inference we call migration---is long assumed in Lyapunov's second method but never characterized at the criterion level. We formalize stability criteria over trajectory families, distinguish admissibility of a criterion (its structural condition suffices for its conclusion) from tightness (its necessity), and establish the necessary and sufficient structural conditions for validity. In logarithmic coordinates the theory reduces to a single two-sided displacement function of the comparison pair: in discrete time, migration holds if and only if a regularity package (excluding failure by infinitely many steps of finite displacement) and a joint lower bound (excluding failure by a single step of unbounded expansion) hold simultaneously. Continuous time strengthens the latter; the two criteria are separated exactly by the minimum step size. Written without its inverse-function formulation, the Panteley--Lor'ia criterion coincides with our continuous-time conditions on every nondecreasing pair, and loses soundness beyond: it was already complete on the classical regularity class. An envelope construction shows that regularization costs no discriminative power, and radial unboundedness, a standing assumption since Hahn, is dispensable.
authors: Yixiang Guo; Lin Tie; Quan Quan

title: Data Center Load Reductions: Attribution, Measurement Limits, and Estimation
summary: Hundreds of gigawatts of data center loads are seeking interconnection in the United States given the massive growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing. In recent years, several incidents of data centers reducing their loads by hundreds to thousands of megawatts have been documented, raising grid reliability concerns. U.S. regulators have since ordered reliability standards for the integration of computational loads, and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) now calls on transmission owners to install disturbance recorders at these facilities to support root cause analysis. Such recorders usually observe only electrical quantities at the point of interconnection (POI). A sudden load reduction can be caused by a change in workload or a switch to backup supply. This work shows when POI measurements can distinguish the two mechanisms. It is established that they can produce identical POI voltage and current in a quasi-static constant power model, and during the transient their separation depends on the reduction relative to measurement noise, the clearing time, the dynamics through which workload reaches the POI, and the recorder bandwidth. When POI data are insufficient, an estimator that uses workload data is proposed to determine how much of the facility stayed connected. The results of this work identify the measurements and grid information utilities need to determine why data center load dropped.
authors: Abdallah Alalem Albustami; Ahmad F. Taha; Mohammad Alwahdanee; Zuhaib Shakeel Muhammad

title: Two-Layer Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC)-Aided Multi-User MIMO Networks
summary: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC)-aided beamforming, which performs signal processing directly in the analog domain, has recently emerged as a promising alternative to fully digital and hybrid beamforming for multi-antenna systems. However, existing studies have shown that a single lossless and reciprocal MiLAC at the transmitter cannot, in general, attain the performance of fully digital beamforming in multi-user scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose a two-layer MiLAC-aided transmit beamforming architecture for downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. Leveraging multiport microwave network theory, we first establish a general physics-compliant model of the proposed architecture, and then derive a simplified model under the assumptions of unilateral and perfectly matched amplifiers. We prove that, with lossless and reciprocal MiLACs, the two-layer MiLAC-aided transmitter can realize any fully digital transmit beamformer, while a single-layer MiLAC-aided receiver can attain the same achievable rate as a fully digital linear combiner. We then derive closed-form mappings from fully digital transmit beamformers and receive combiners to their corresponding MiLAC-aided analog implementations. Based on these equivalence results, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem for the considered multi-user MIMO network and develop an optimization framework for jointly designing the power allocation and scattering matrices of the MiLAC-aided transceivers. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and show that the proposed two-layer MiLAC-aided design attains the same sum-rate performance as its fully digital counterpart.
authors: Xiaohua Zhou; Tianyu Fang; Matteo Nerini; Yijie Mao; Bruno Clerckx

title: Machine learning-guided real-time AC optimal transmission switching
summary: The operation of power grids has substantial economic consequences, affecting generation costs and, ultimately, electricity prices. The Optimal Transmission Switching (OTS) problem seeks to reduce these costs by selectively switching off transmission lines. However, OTS gives rise to a challenging mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that is difficult to solve at operationally relevant timescales, particularly as rapidly changing loads create a need for real-time switching decisions. To address this challenge, we develop a machine learning-guided method that identifies high quality line switching decisions in real time. Specifically, we construct a grid-specific switching-value model that rapidly estimates the generation-cost reduction associated with opening transmission lines by fine-tuning a pretrained model for AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF). The switching-value model provides signals to guide promising switching decisions, and topologies proposed by the model are evaluated using exact AC-OPF solvers to verify feasibility and obtain the actual generation cost. We develop multiple strategies that use the ML surrogate to efficiently explore the combinatorial space of transmission topologies, including Fixed-Rank Search, Adaptive-Rank Search, and Swap-Enhanced Search. Across multiple benchmark networks, our proposed algorithms identify line switching decisions that significantly reduce generation cost within a 50s computational budget. In particular, under a realistic data center buildout scenario on the 2,000-bus synthetic Texas grid, our approach reduces generation costs by 31.97% and gross nodal load payments by 94.34%. More broadly, our results demonstrate that a fine-tuned surrogate can effectively guide search even without guaranteeing feasibility, enabling classical optimization methods to tackle large nonlinear combinatorial problems on operationally relevant timescales.
authors: Weimin Huang; Weiwei Yang; Bistra Dilkina; Konstantina Mellou; Ishai Menache; Marco Molinaro; Chris White; Baosen Zhang

title: Physics-Guided Inferencer-in-the-Loop Digital-Twin for Real-Time Adaptive Emulation of Nonlinear PMSMs
summary: A real-time digital-twin (RTDT) of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) allows drive controllers to be tested in hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) before they meet the real machine. Its machine model rests on identified parameters or flux look-up tables (LUTs) from finite-element analysis (FEA) or characterization tests; the maps are regenerated offline when the machine changes, and online estimators track a few parameters such as resistance and PM flux. This article makes the executed model learnable from reference data. A physics-guided machine learning (PGML) network advances the currents and predicts torque in one step, trained with analytical one-step labels. In the proposed Inferencer-in-the-Loop (IIL) architecture, a GPU retrains the network while a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) executes the last accepted weights. For damper circuits, shifted parameters, and an FEA-calibrated saturated machine, one kernel form reaches average normalized mean absolute errors (NMAEs) of 0.19%-0.67% at measured FPGA kernel latencies of 0.30-0.34 $μ$s, and retraining for a shifted machine nears its final loss within 94 s. On a magnetically linear 200-W drive, a residual form corrects the analytical step and learns its physical parameters from operating data; each step takes under 2.5 $μ$s, 20 times faster than real time and ahead of the physical drive's measurements even at 20-kHz sampling. On six held-out runs (1193 s), its $i_q$ error is 5.9%-9.4% of measured RMS, against 10.4%-13.2% for an independently fitted grey-box model, and over 30 min of loaded heating its online-updated heads track a 4.1% winding-resistance rise with an RMS error of 0.44 m$Ω$.
authors: Songyang Zhang; Yuzhong Zhang; Venkata Dinavahi

title: Passive Identification of Unequal Phase Grid Impedances by Phase-Domain Source Cancellation
summary: Passive grid impedance estimators that return a single resistance--inductance pair cannot represent a grid whose phase impedances are unequal. This paper identifies a separate pair for each phase from recorded point-of-common-coupling (PCC) voltage and current without injected perturbations. In each phase, the unknown grid-source voltage is cancelled by a periodic difference (PD) or by a second-order-generalized-integrator notch difference (SOGID), and moving-window integration (MWI) replaces the current derivative by an integral and an endpoint feature. The resulting two-parameter regression requires a period or notch-frequency estimate but no phase-locked-loop angle. A voltage-balance analysis gives the source residual left by frequency mismatch and bounds the parameter error by the ratio of this residual to the conditioning of the two features. In the unequal-phase interval (8.3--9.8~s) of a 10-s EMTP grid-forming record, SOGID-MWI attains phase-averaged R/L errors of 5.09/0.33\%; a shared value has a minimum error of 41.67\% for the phase ratio 1:0.5:2. On a 50-s constant-impedance grid-following record, the errors are 0.56/0.06\% over the 20--30-s synchronization disturbance. In a controlled 40-dB noise study, a noise-referenced update rule reduces the white-noise GFL error from 55.9/65.0\% to 12.3/11.5\%.
authors: Songyang Zhang; Xun Gong; Bo Cao; Reza Iravani

title: Covariance Learning for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation with Sparse Linear Arrays
summary: Covariance learning (CL) estimates source powers and sensor-noise variance by minimizing the Type-II (marginal) negative log-likelihood of the array measurements. We develop both grid-based and gridless CL direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimators applicable to arbitrary sparse linear array (SLA) geometries. The grid-based DOA estimator minimizes the Type-II objective on an angular grid via successive convex approximation (SCA) and estimates the noise variance by a scalar bisection search. The gridless DOA estimator then refines each grid-based DOA over the continuum using a Newton method. Simulations on a six-sensor nested array, including an underdetermined case with nine sources, show that the proposed DOA estimators outperform state-of-the-art methods, despite jointly estimating the sensor noise variance.
authors: Majdoddin Esfandiari; Esa Ollila; Geert Leus; Daniel P. Palomar

title: Looping Kooshball: Improved k-space coverage for silent fMRI using 3D coherence trajectories
summary: Functional MRI (fMRI) is widely used to characterize brain activity and connectivity, but conventional gradient-echo echo-planar imaging produces high acoustic sound-pressure levels by operating gradient hardware near its limits. Scanner noise can increase anxiety and motion, particularly in noise-sensitive populations, and can evoke auditory responses that confound both task-based and resting-state measurements. Looping Star (LS) is a near-silent, T2*-weighted acquisition that uses slowly varying gradients and multiplexed, temporally staggered coherences. Conventional LS rotates planar encoding trajectories across shots to achieve three-dimensional coverage. Because these planes intersect near the center of k-space, sampling is dense at low spatial frequencies but sparse and nonuniform at the periphery, limiting efficiency when relatively few shots are combined for high temporal resolution. We introduce Looping Kooshball (LKB), a complementary LS trajectory that extends through all three spatial dimensions within each shot. LKB is designed to improve volumetric k-space coverage while preserving the echo-formation and coherence-crushing properties of LS. We compare LKB with conventional LS using point-spread-function analysis, in-bore acoustic measurements, structural phantom imaging, and preliminary visual-motor fMRI experiments. We evaluate whether LKB reduces undersampling artifacts and improves temporal stability and functional-activation detection without sacrificing the near-silent operation of LS.
authors: David J. Frey; Shreya Ramachandran; Jeffrey A. Fessler; Douglas C. Noll; Tobias C. Wood

title: State-Dependent Delay Modeling of Wind-Farm Wake Dynamics
summary: Turbines convert wind to electrical power. In the wake of a turbine, wind speed is reduced in proportion to the amount of power extracted. In a wind farm, downstream turbines may be located in wake of an upstream turbine, requiring coordination to yield maximum power generation. This paper creates a state-dependent delay model for a two turbine wind farm. The upstream turbine creates a wake that diminishes the wind speed at the downstream turbine. Changing the upstream turbine operation will affect the downstream turbine after a delay that depends on the wind-propagation time between them. This delay depends on the upstream power extraction and it can destabilize the combined dynamics. Conventional models of this effect rely on nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Control design and analysis with such models is difficult with established methods. We first show that the PDE model can be represented by an Abel-type state-dependent delay differential equation. The equation has an implicit solution. To obtain an explicit representation, we then introduce a simplified state-dependent delay model. Both models predict destabilizing interactions between the two turbines. Numerical examples illustrate delay-induced oscillations using the simplified model and verify their effectiveness in simulation.
authors: Sengiyumva Kisole; Jungbae Chun; Peter Seiler; Matthew M. Peet

title: Improving the Dependency on Fine-Tuning Data in Transfer Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition
summary: Compensating for train-test mismatches in acoustic environments is important for deployable speech solutions. This paper proposes to reduce the amount of fine-tuning data needed in transfer learning to mitigate the train-test mismatch by using a compensation mechanism based on the feature maximum likelihood linear regression (fMLLR) algorithm. Our scheme incorporates an autoencoder to reduce the number of trainable parameters. Operating on the encoder latent space, our compensation strategy employs an affine linear transform that accounts for rotations and shifts in the feature space. We evaluate the proposed solution in a speech emotion recognition (SER) task within a realistic human-robot interaction scenario. The results show that the proposed architecture outperforms the original scheme without the compensation strategy. We observe a performance gain in the mean concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of 16.8% using 12.9% of the training set, and 14.4% using 50% of the training set.
authors: Ricardo García; Rodrigo Mahu; Carlos Busso; Néstor Becerra Yoma

title: Forward-Backward Map Matching for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
summary: Airborne magnetic anomaly navigation provides a passive, unjammable alternative to Global Navigation Satellite Systems positioning by matching magnetometer measurements against a lithospheric magnetic anomaly map. Existing map-matching algorithms either assume a Gaussian posterior (extended Kalman filter), require Monte Carlo sampling (particle filter), or discard posterior uncertainty in favour of a single optimal path (Viterbi algorithm). Here we formulate map matching as inference on a chain-structured factor graph and solve it segment by segment using the forward-backward algorithm, which yields a discrete posterior over candidate positions and its Shannon entropy $H_t$ at time $t$. Over the \texttt{Renfrew\_395} map, $10^3$ synthetic trials yield a median position error of $32.7$ m, $91\%$ below the median inertial drift of $362$ m. On these trials and $10^3$ flight paths, the median error is $43\%$ below the extended Kalman filter and particle filter. Across these paths, a threshold on segment-level entropy detects $47\%$ of segments with errors above two map cells and $94\%$ of those above three, at a $10\%$ false-alarm rate. The foregoing results indicate that $H_t$ provides a truth-free diagnostic of map-conditioned navigation ambiguity.
authors: Joseph O'Leary; Tapio Simula; Tom Kimpson; Corey Davey; Wenchao Li; Andrew D. Greentree; Allison Kealy

title: A Subsample Time-Delay Estimator with a Farrow Structure
summary: A novel solution to the classical problem of subsample time-delay estimation (TDE) for a wideband signal received by two adjacent sensors is described. A mean squared-error (MSE) measure of dissimilarity is defined and evaluated using a variable fractional-delay (VFD) filter bank with a finite impulse response (FIR). Using a filter bank with a Farrow structure allows the MSE power to be expressed as a polynomial function of the filter delay with a local minimum at the unknown signal delay. In Monte-Carlo simulations, the proposed estimator outperforms the generalized cross-correlation (GCC) technique when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is not low (less than 10 dB).
authors: Hugh L. Kennedy

title: ODAQ-Collection: Expanding the Open Dataset of Audio Quality with a Focus on Spatial Distortions
summary: The Open Dataset of Audio Quality (ODAQ) is an expanding resource that addresses the scarcity of openly available data in audio quality assessment research. While previous contributions focused mainly on timbral distortions, with spatial processing limited to basic mid-side and left-right stereo conditions, we present a new contribution featuring high-quality music and speech recordings with diverse stereo images, controlled spatial distortions, and subjective listening test results from trained listeners in a laboratory setting. With 148 pairs of stereo audio samples processed by three different method classes, two applying controlled binaural cue distortions and one applying dialogue enhancement, this addition expands the collection to 688 pairs of processed and unprocessed audio signals spanning 17 processing method classes, along with 18,984 raw subjective ratings from listeners. All associated data and code are released as open resources to facilitate future expansions and research on objective audio quality metrics.
authors: Chih-Wei Wu; Matteo Torcoli; Mhd Modar Halimeh; Pablo M. Delgado; Sascha Dick; Christoph Thompson; Phillip A. Williams; Emanuël A. P. Habets

title: Neuroscience of Improvisation Across Music and Other Domains: A Survey and Outlook
summary: Improvisation (or Improv), the real-time generation of novel, context-appropriate action, occurs in music, dance, theater, sport, education, therapy, and professional practice. Its neuroscience, however, has been studied almost exclusively for music, where most quantitative neuroimaging evidence lies. A PRISMA-style search done by authors quantifies this imbalance: of 111 identified studies, 70.3\% concern musical improvisation or general psychometric creativity. This explains why earlier surveys are either music-centered or confined to a single construct. This survey addresses that gap in two ways. First, for music, it organizes findings from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), hyperscanning, neurofeedback, and brain stimulation, and reports transparently where the evidence agrees (e.g., experience-dependent changes in frontal engagement, increased frontal alpha and theta power) and where it is heterogeneous (e.g., the direction of lateral prefrontal activity, hemispheric lateralization, the interpretation of alpha power). Second, it extends the review to dance, theater, sport, education, therapy, and professional practice, where behavioral, qualitative, and simulation-based studies predominate. Overall, the current evidence does not point to a universal neural signature of improvisation within music domain or other domains. We conclude with an outlook on wearable EEG--fNIRS sensing and closed-loop brain--computer interfaces for musical improvisation, the domain with sufficient evidence, formulated as an expertise-gated control problem and discussed as a possible complement to deliberate practice, and we list the evidence needed for other domains.
authors: Levina Perzhilla; Muhammad Mahboob Ur Rahman; Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri

title: Doppler-Shannon Association in Vehicular Networks: A Stochastic Geometry Analysis
summary: Historically, in cellular networks, the user equipment (UE) association with a base station (BS) has been largely confined to nearest BS association strategies. Unlike cellular networks wherein the BSs are static, vehicular networks are prone to high mobility, resulting in the UE experiencing a Doppler shift. The Doppler shift further results in the fading channel exhibiting high temporal variability. In this work, we present a novel stochastic geometry framework, modeling the effects of the Doppler shift on the physical layer network performance through the coherence time. First, the statistics of the Doppler shift are studied in a two- and three-dimensional Poisson point process (PPP) setting. The distribution and the geometric factors influencing the Doppler shift are analyzed. Next, we propose Doppler shift aware utilities, modeling the Doppler shift induced Shannon rate achievable in time-selective fading links. Through these utilities, we analytically study the outage and coverage probabilities for a UE to achieve a given quality of service. These probabilities are computed based on the optimal BS association in vehicular networks, which goes beyond the closest Euclidean distance. In the UE-BS line of sight, the novel BS association policies factor the BS direction of motion and the fading gain, in addition to the Euclidean distance. We show that the nearest BS is no longer the optimal BS association, resulting in non-convex coverage tessellations associated with the BSs. Our analytical and simulation results illustrate the need for a Doppler shift correction, complementing the ideal SNR based Shannon performance. The network performance achieved through the proposed Doppler-Shannon based association is proved, analytically as well as through simulations, to be superior to the classical Shannon based association.
authors: Ashutosh Balakrishnan; Francois Baccelli; Sanjoy Kumar Jhawar; Philippe Martins

title: Beyond Utterance-Level Speaker Similarity: Perception-Aligned Segmental Evaluation of Accent in Speech Generation
summary: Utterance-level similarity ratings do not reveal where perceived accent differences occur in generated speech. We introduce a segmental evaluation protocol combining speaker and accent similarity ratings with subword annotations of perceived accent differences provided by listeners from target accent regions. Using newly collected recordings, 47 retained listeners evaluate 200 content-matched reference--candidate pairs spanning four Scottish and Australian voices, two zero-shot TTS systems, and an articulation-based voice conversion system. Subword annotations locate salient pronunciation differences and sometimes yield different system rankings from similarity ratings. Speaker and accent ratings remain strongly associated ($ρ= 0.71$), highlighting the value of examining local perceptual evidence beyond these scores. Evaluation of seven objective distances reveals weak correspondence with subword selections, with correlations reaching at most $ρ= 0.22$. We release code, data, and an interactive demo to support the development of perceptually grounded segmental accent evaluation.
authors: Jinzuomu Zhong; Alice Ross; Catherine Lai; Korin Richmond

title: Robust Dynamic Safety Margins are Robust Control Barrier Functions
summary: This paper establishes robustness properties for control barrier functions (CBFs) constructed using dynamic safety margins (DSMs). We show that DSMs can act as robust CBFs by leveraging input-to-state stability for Lyapunov-based constructions, and contractivity for trajectory-prediction-based approaches. Additionally, we derive closed-form DSM-based robust CBFs (RDSM-RCBFs) specifically for linear systems. Simulations highlight the improved robustness of the proposed RDSM-RCBFs compared to nominal DSM-CBF baselines.
authors: Victor Freire; Saber Jafarpour; Marco M. Nicotra

title: Efficient Joint Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Secure UAV Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in wireless networks; however, ensuring secure communication and efficient energy usage remains challenging. This paper addresses the joint trajectory optimization and resource allocation problem in UAV networks in the presence of a tethered UAV flying center and a malicious ground eavesdropper. In the proposed model, UAVs are equipped with energy harvesting capabilities and can adaptively switch between transmitting, jamming, and relaying roles to deliver data to a tethered UAV center for optimized network performance. An optimization problem is formulated to maximize a utility function that balances secrecy rate, energy consumption, and interference. To address the high non-convexity of the problem and its real-time decision requirements, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed to solve the problem and learn the network dynamics. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior secrecy performance, lower energy consumption, and reduced interference compared to conventional and DRL-based methods.
authors: Abdulmalik Alwarafy; Mohamed Hayajneh; Mustafa Al Juboori; Abdulaziz Almarzooqi; Tahnoon Almazrouei; Robera Abera; Kaleab Nega

title: A Community Impact-Centered Network Reduction Method for Power Systems Resilience Planning
summary: Power systems resilience planning requires evaluating many hazard scenarios and investment portfolios, often requiring network reduction for computational tractability. The resulting aggregation, however, can obscure community impact data needed for equitable planning. We present a network reduction method that jointly preserves network physics and the spatial distribution of community data. We embed a household-level scarce resource score that characterizes outage impact within optimization-based Kron reductions with two formulations: a scarcity-weighted method that prioritizes vulnerable nodes, and a scarcity-constrained method that bounds data dissimilarity within aggregated clusters. Both are evaluated on a realistic distribution feeder of Galveston Island, Texas and benchmarked against multiple approaches. The scarcity-constrained method performs best, achieving 86% reduction with worst-case voltage errors below 0.01p.u. while preserving the spatial distribution of community data. By explicitly controlling data heterogeneity within and across clusters, the proposed method yields reduced networks that retain decision-relevant community information without sacrificing electrical accuracy.
authors: Jiarui Gao; Abigail L. Beck; Rabab Haider

title: Flow Matching for Fluctuation-Based Fluorescence Super-Resolution
summary: Fluctuation-based super-resolution techniques are an appealing alternative to single-molecule and structured-illumination microscopy, as they adapt to standard acquisition settings and exploit the independent stochastic fluctuations of fluorophores across a sequence of frames. However, most existing approaches lack an explicit model of the acquisition process and provide only relative intensity estimates, limiting quantitative analyses. In this work, we combine model-based and generative approaches to exploit the full stochastic information in the sequence, proposing a reconstruction framework built on flow matching and a double-Poisson forward model accounting for blinking, blur, under-sampling and noise. The method alternates two steps: a flow matching model first learns the distribution of the acquired data; then, the sample and the background are jointly estimated by minimising a Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and simulated distributions via regularised proximal gradient steps. On simulated and real Argolight data, the method resolves lines separated by 120 nm, outperforming SACD and eSRRF.
authors: Alberto Cozzani; Giacomo Meanti; Laure Blanc-Féraud; Luca Calatroni

title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis
summary: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) characterizes the local frequency content of time-varying signals by evaluating the discrete Fourier transform over a sliding analysis window. The STFT is governed by a fundamental resolution trade-off: a short window localizes rapid transients in time at the cost of frequency resolution, whereas a long window resolves closely spaced harmonics at the expense of temporal resolution. The Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform (U-STFT) resolves this trade-off sequentially by modeling the analysis window duration as a data-adaptive state variable that indexes the number of hops included in the current observation interval. At each frame, a bank of candidate window durations is scored using normalized order-three Rényi entropy to quantify joint time-frequency concentration. A window length trellis aggregates the resulting $\mathcal{O}(3^M)$ candidate window schedules with linear complexity per frame, guaranteeing a cumulative mix-loss regret bound of $\mathcal{O}((k+1)\log M)$ relative to any hindsight window schedule with $k$ resolution changes over $M$ frames. By linearity of the Fourier transform, posterior expectation across the candidate bank yields a single spectrum equivalent to an STFT evaluated with a data-adaptive effective window, while an envelope-normalized synthesis stream guarantees exact overlap-add reconstruction. Evaluations on synthetic and marine bioacoustic signals demonstrate adaptive resolution tracking, enhanced spectral concentration, and exact time-domain invertibility.
authors: Manan Mittal; Kanad Sarkar; Ryan M. Corey; John R. Buck; Andrew C. Singer

title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: real-time algorithms
summary: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.
authors: Saugat Shahi; Jonathan Frey; Filippo Fabiani; Moritz Diehl; Mario Zanon

title: Longitudinal retinal imaging and auxiliary tasks for discrete-time survival prediction of referable diabetic retinopathy and maculopathy: a retrospective cohort study
summary: Deep learning can predict progression to referable diabetic retinopathy (rDR) and referable maculopathy (rM) from screening photographs, but existing models ignore the prior images that screening programmes hold. We assessed whether multi-visit (MV) images and auxiliary objectives that model the future visit improve prognostic prediction. In this retrospective cohort study of macula-centred photographs from the South-East London Diabetic Eye Screening Programme (UK), eyes without referable disease at baseline and with a follow-up at 20-28 months were split into development (72,559 eyes, 36,648 patients) and test (17,917 eyes, 9,071 patients) sets. A time-aware discrete-time survival model predicted incident rDR (R2 or R3), rM (M1), or either (rDR/rM). We compared baseline-only input with up to three visits (MV), alone or with auxiliary supervision of future-visit age (MV+age) or future-visit latent prediction (MV+latent), using the AUROC of 28-month cumulative risk and paired DeLong tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In the test set, 308 eyes (1.7%) developed rDR/rM, 58 (0.3%) rDR, and 275 (1.5%) rM. MV images increased the AUROC for rDR/rM from 0.749 to 0.786 (+0.037, 95% CI 0.012-0.061; q=0.011) and for rM from 0.749 to 0.788 (+0.039, 0.013-0.065; q=0.010). Auxiliary objectives did not improve MV model performance. In eyes with two or three visits, prior visits accounted for 30-38% of positive Grad-CAM attributions. Prior screening images improved prediction of incident maculopathy and the composite rDR/rM outcome, with gains driven by longitudinal images, not auxiliary supervision. External validation and prospective studies are required before the deployment of models to individualise screening.
authors: Paul Nderitu; Laura Webster; Samantha S. Mann; Christos Bergeles; Timothy L. Jackson

title: A Theory of Transmit-Receive-Manifold of Single-Photon Quantum-Dot Antenna Arrays
summary: A quantum-dot array that receives a single photon is a collectively coupled antenna, and its receive manifold is not always the plane-wave manifold. So, this work aims to develop a complete transmit-channel-receive manifold model for quantum dot (QD) arrays. For the sake of validation, it considers a reference target pattern which can be obtained using classical array excitation.
authors: Angeru Pavan Kumar; Sandip Ghosal

title: An Open-Source Hybrid Ray-Tracing and 3GPP Channel Simulator for Non-Terrestrial Network
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid channel simulation framework that combines site-specific ray tracing (RT) with 3GPP-compliant statistical channel simulation for non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The proposed approach uses RT to generate dominant propagation paths and augments them with statistically generated paths and subpaths to provide richer multipath realizations under practical simulation complexity. To provide a complete simulation framework, we integrate Sionna RT, 3GPP, and hybrid RT-3GPP simulators within a unified workflow. Simulation results based on key channel statistics and power delay profiles show that the proposed method preserves site-specific propagation characteristics while providing sufficiently rich multipath components, thereby addressing the complementary limitations of conventional RT-based and purely statistical NTN channel simulators. The developed simulator is also released as an open-source project to support reproducibility and further NTN research.
authors: Yu-Chien Lin; Cheng-Yi Chang; Yen-Cheng Lai; Ming-Chun Lee; Ta-Sung Lee

title: EUReCA: End-to-End Unified CBCT Reconstruction Across Clinical Acquisitions
summary: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used for image-guided radiotherapy, but reducing the number of projections to lower dose and scan time makes reconstruction increasingly ill-posed. We present EUReCA (End-to-end Unified REconstruction across Clinical Acquisitions), a geometry-aware feed-forward model for variable-view clinical linac CBCT. For a given acquisition trajectory, EUReCA accepts 8-100 projections with a single set of weights, without view-count-specific retraining; the same architecture and training recipe extend unchanged to other clinical trajectories. It combines learned projection features with an in-frame Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstruction. The model encodes each projection with a shared multiscale backbone, back-projects features into multiresolution 3D grids using the acquisition geometry, aggregates variable numbers of views at fixed computational cost, and refines the volume with a global 3D transformer and multilevel decoder. On simulated data, EUReCA achieved 29.9-33.2 dB PSNR with 10-100 views and outperformed all applicable feed-forward baselines; it also exceeded iterative optimization-based methods while running orders of magnitude faster. On 15 measured patient CBCT scans evaluated against vendor reconstructions, EUReCA achieved the best performance at every tested view count. These results suggest that geometry-aware, measurement-anchored feed-forward reconstruction can provide a practical and flexible foundation for variable-view linac CBCT.
authors: Jiening Zhu; Chengzhu Zhang; Jason Fan; LiCheng Kuo; Weixing Cai; Xiuxiu He; Laura Cervino; Jean Moran; Xiang Li; Tianfang Li; Yabo Fu

title: Coordinated and Uncoordinated Channel Tracking for High-Rate IoT in Distributed Massive MIMO With Low-Resolution ADCs
summary: This paper investigates dynamic channel tracking for high-rate Internet of things (IoT) in distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) with low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), where pilot and data activities are decoupled, pilots are reused, and mobile channels evolve across access slots. We hereby develop a quantization-aware joint coordinated Kalman filter (Q-JCKF) for known pilot activity and a quantization-aware distributed probabilistic data association filter (Q-DPDAF) for uncoordinated access. For uplink analysis, we derive a closed-form statistical use-and-then-forget (UatF) expression for Q-JCKF and mixture-aware, pilot-conditioned, and long-term statistical UatF formulations for Q-DPDAF, together with the large-N pilot-reuse ceiling and a cross-access point (AP) association term with an O(epsilon) posterior-concentration bound. The proposed framework recovers JC-KF/PDAF in the ideal-ADC co-located limit, and quantifies the conditional loss of Kalman measurement information caused by finite-resolution quantization. We further characterize computational, memory, and fronthaul scaling: Kronecker-structured Q-JCKF reduces covariance-processing complexity, while groupwise Q-DPDAF limits hypothesis enumeration from 2^K to 2^{K_r} and enables parallel AP-local processing. Simulations corroborate the analytical and complexity outcomes, quantify ADC-resolution and pilot-access effects, and demonstrate improved lower-tail spectral efficiency, robust mobility tracking, near-ideal 4-bit performance, reliable Q-DPDAF activity inference, and substantial runtime reductions over legacy implementations and processing frameworks.
authors: Hediyeh Soltanizadeh; Ardavan Rahimian

title: 5G Sensing for Human Pose Estimation with PRS-based CSI: An Experimental Demonstration
summary: This paper presents an experimental study of device- free 2D human pose estimation using Channel State Information (CSI) extracted from downlink Fifth Generation (5G) Positioning Reference Signal (PRS). The proposed system employs a Next Generation Node Base (gNB) transmitting PRS to a User Equipment (UE) equipped with two receive antennas to measure the radio channel. The CSI is estimated using a least-squares (LS) method, and processed through amplitude smoothing and phase calibration. The resulting amplitude and phase representations are used as inputs to a deep learning model for pose estimation. We compare amplitude-only input with joint amplitude-phase training at a bandwidth of 20 MHz. The joint training outperforms the amplitude-only solution and achieves Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) equal to 32.2%, 72.9%, and 84.2% below 10%, 30%, and 50% of the distance between left shoulder and right hip, respectively. These results demonstrate that standardized downlink 5G PRS-based CSI contains useful information for human pose estimation, even with a simple radio configuration and a relatively small dataset.
authors: Zhaorui Yin; Pietro Morri; Mattia Brambilla; Monica Nicoli

title: Joint Antenna Positioning and Pilot Power Allocation for Uplink Fluid Antenna-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
summary: This paper investigates joint fluid antenna (FA) position optimization and pilot power allocation for uplink cell-free massive MIMO networks supporting ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) traffic under pilot contamination. By continuously adjusting FA elements within a prescribed aperture, we adapt the spatial correlation structure to the varying propagation environment. We formulate a joint problem to minimize the average normalized mean-squared error (NMSE) subject to QoS constraints governed by finite blocklength and Markov-modulated Poisson process queueing analyses. To ensure tractability, we establish an analytical quadratic relationship between the NMSE and the effective signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio through eigenstructure alignment factors. This mapping translates complex latency requirements into explicit NMSE thresholds, maintaining a median absolute approximation error below 0.03 dB and less than 10% relative error for over 90% of practical-regime samples. Given the nonconvex nature of the formulation, we propose an alternating optimization framework. Antenna positions are iteratively updated via successive convex approximation using analytical gradients and closed-form Euclidean projections. Pilot powers are allocated through a block coordinate descent scheme that employs safeguarded Newton steps to guarantee monotonic convergence. Furthermore, we introduce an auto-calibrated regularization variant to navigate the Pareto frontier between estimation accuracy and energy consumption. Numerical results show the proposed positioning yields up to 22% NMSE improvement over fixed uniform arrays while operating 7-8x faster than particle swarm optimization. The power allocation achieves within 0.5% of the global optimum at over two orders of magnitude lower computational cost, providing up to 39% pilot energy reduction with negligible estimation penalty.
authors: Manobendu Sarker; Soumaya Cherkaoui

title: Assessing BIOMASS Radiometric Stability using Permanent Scatterers
summary: Monitoring the relative radiometric stability of the European Space Agency's BIOMASS P-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) requires separating instrumental and processing effects from temporal changes in the scene backscatter. This study investigates the use of permanent scatterers (PSs) as opportunistic references for estimating residual radiometric gains without dedicated calibration targets. The PS-based calibration (PSCal) framework combines amplitude-based scatterer selection with iterative maximum-likelihood gain estimation. Simulations assess detection and estimation performance under the limited number of acquisitions available in BIOMASS stacks, highlighting the importance of stringent selection thresholds and the dependence of estimation accuracy on scatterer abundance and signal-to-noise ratio. The approach is applied to datasets over Nairobi, Kenya, and Cordoba, Argentina.
