A network with separate weights for each subcarrier lowered the bit error rate by 14 to 22% with its training pilot but raised it by 2 to 18% with every other pilot tested, and longer training widened this gap. A convolutional neural receiver following an open-source tutorial gained 37 percentage points more on its training pilot than on unseen pilots after short training, and 9 points more after nine times longer training, much of which also appeared with a linear amplifier. The gap shrank with amplifier back-off but persisted where the in-band distortion meets the 5G limit. On a channel with short delay spread, smoothing the channel estimate across subcarriers without training lowered the error rate on all 107 pilot sequences tested, by 30% on average. Learned receivers should therefore be tested on unseen pilots and against such simple baselines.
authors: Mohammad Tasin; Al Imran

title: A 140.5$μ$W, 99.8% Accuracy, 96.1dB SNR BioZ IC for Real-Time Cell Analysis with On-Demand Push-Pull Excitation and Continuous-Time $ΔΣ$ T-D Readout
summary: This paper presents a bioimpedance IC combining an on-demand push-pull driver and continuous-time $ΔΣ$ T-D readout to address the trade-off between SNR, accuracy and power consumption. The driver delivers 200$μ$App with $\leq$0.14% THD while consuming 80.3$μ$A. Using a 6MHz clock, the readout achieves 53.6ps effective timing resolution at a 4k$Ω$ load (0.1-4Hz noise integration). The IC achieves 96.1dB peak SNR, 99.8% magnitude accuracy and 0.13$^{\circ}$ phase error at a maximum power consumption of 140.5$μ$W.
authors: Jiayang Li; Junzhe Chen; Xin Zhang; Peiqing Li; Liwen Zhang; Navya Nayak; Yating Zou; Xuanyu Liang; Hubin Zhao; Roshan Weerasekera; Xiao Liu; Reza Haqshenas; Dai Jiang; Martin Cryan; Sohmyung Ha; Andreas Demosthenous; Edoardo Charbon; Dinesh Pamunuwa

title: Semantic-Guided Frequency Modulation for Learned Image Compression
summary: High-frequency attenuation can reduce the rate of learned image codecs but also remove object boundaries and fine detail. We propose Semantic-Guided Adaptive Latent-Frequency Modulation (SG-AFM), which uses a semantic structural prior to guide attenuation of encoder latents. SG-AFM applies a Haar wavelet transform and combines a fixed semantic-frequency multiplier with a bounded learned correction to modulate high-frequency subbands. The semantic prior is computed only at the encoder. No semantic map is transmitted, and no decoder modules are added. Across six datasets, SG-AFM reduces PSNR-based BD-rate relative to TCM by an average of 13.17%. It achieves the best BD-rate among the compared methods on ExDark, NightCity, and OnePlus, with a mean reduction of 16.80%. An ablation on OnePlus demonstrates the benefit of spatially aligned semantic guidance, and visual comparisons illustrate improved reconstruction of local structures.
authors: Gangyi Tian; Wen Ji; Alireza Furutanpey; Mingxuan Li

title: Complex Domain Inverse Problem Formulation for 4D Flow MRI Super-Resolution
summary: Four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging measures blood velocity fields in three dimensions throughout the cardiac cycle and is increasingly used to assess hemodynamics. However, these measurements are limited by low signal-to-noise ratios and limited spatial resolution, which can compromise their accuracy and reliability. To address these limitations, we investigate the feasibility of spatial resolution enhancement through a complex-domain inverse problem formulation inspired by MRI acquisition principles. Three inversion methods are evaluated: a closed-form approach (FSR), a Plug-and-Play alternating direction method of multipliers (PnP-ADMM), and a pretrained network that takes the forward operator as input (RAM). On simulated data, all three methods outperform 4DFlowNet at x2 and x4 super-resolution factors. On aortic phantom data at x2 super-resolution, PnP-ADMM and RAM achieve lower root-mean-square error than 4DFlowNet in almost all cases. These results highlight the potential of the proposed formulation and support further development and validation.
authors: Aurélien de Turenne; Denis Kouamé

title: Nodal Inertia Pricing for RoCoF Security with Integration of Synchronous and Virtual Resources
summary: Frequency regulation is becoming a more significant challenge in the undergoing low-carbon transition of modern power systems, which is heavily rely on system inertia provision. In the context of market-based energy allocation, reasonable valuation of the system inertia is crucial to its procurement, namely a worthy price should be determined for inertia providers. However, current research on the value of inertia remains insufficient, particularly during the initial phase immediately following a contingency, a critical period when the system primarily relies on the inherent inertia from conventional units and pre-engaged virtual inertia resources. Furthermore, it is found in existing studies that the Center of Inertia (COI) models exhibit significant deviations from actual physical conditions. For market-oriented reforms that explore individual differences, COI models also fail to capture the heterogeneous contributions of inertia at different nodes to system security. Given these circumstances, this paper proposes a nodal inertia pricing mechanism via a day-ahead unit commitment and inertia co-optimization model with nodal resolution. Following the proposed pricing scheme, the day- or hour-ahead inertia provision is monetized and promoted, providing regional guidance to units and devices with virtual inertia provision, which is further verified by simulation results of the South East Australia Power System.
authors: Bomiao Liang; Yu Yang; Licheng Wang; Lei Wan; Dipti Srinivasan; Fushuan Wen; Youbing Zhang; Beiping Hou

title: Hybrid-time PINNs: Discontinuity-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Learning Hybrid Dynamical Systems
summary: Hybrid dynamical systems flow continuously but jump at discrete events. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) fit data while enforcing known dynamics, but a single network is smooth in time and cannot model these jumps. We show that the more closely a PINN follows a jump, the larger its physics loss must be. We propose hybrid-time PINNs (HT-PINNs), which assign one network to each flow interval of the hybrid time domain and train the networks jointly with the jump times and the unknown parameters. The number of jumps and the sequence of modes are found by enumeration. HT-PINNs recover the number of jumps and the restitution coefficient of a bouncing ball. In a MuJoCo simulation of robotic disassembly, where a robot pulls a press-fitted pin out of a housing through a spring, HT-PINNs find the number of jumps and the sequence of modes, and estimate the static and kinetic friction coefficients with small errors of 0.1% and 1.7%.
authors: Shivanshu Tripathi; Maziar Raissi

title: Cross-View and Cross-Time Tracking of Crack Evolution in Concrete
summary: Crack propagation provides richer information than static crack observations for evaluating structural conditions of concrete infrastructure and planning maintenance strategies. Unlike static crack detection, which can now be largely automated using computer vision, vision-based crack tracking is a coupled cross-view and cross-time problem: the same physical crack must retain its identity as camera viewpoints change, while newly developed growth must be distinguished from existing crack segments in a unified reference view. Existing segmentation and 3D reconstruction methods can recover crack masks or scene geometry, but they do not preserve crack identity across views or quantify temporal extension. To address this gap, this study formulates crack growth monitoring as a cross-view and cross-time crack-instance tracking task and proposes a geometry-assisted, morphology-aware framework. The framework first uses image-based geometric registration to align observations from different viewpoints into a shared structural reference, then applies morphology-aware instantiation to assign physically interpretable crack identities, and finally performs temporal mapping in the unified view to distinguish newly developed growth from existing crack segments. To enable evaluation, a temporally annotated dataset was established and used, covering three representative cracking scenarios: single dominant crack propagation, mixed-mode branching, and multiple-crack interaction, with pixel-level masks and cross-time instance labels. Experimental results show that the proposed framework can establish loose cross-view identity correspondence under changing viewpoints, while strict spatial overlap and growth localization remain limited by early micro-crack segmentability and projection drift, highlighting directions for future crack-monitoring research.
authors: Pengru Deng; Jiapeng Yao; Su Wang; Xuhui He; Zhao Wang; Takanori Emaru; Takashi Matsumoto; Xinrun Li

title: Cross-Band Movable-Antenna Communications under Frequency-Dependent Multipath
summary: Movable antennas (MAs) provide additional spatial degrees of freedom by adapting their physical positions to the propagation environment. However, existing studies mainly focus on single-band or contiguous wideband transmission, leaving the cross-band spatial behavior of MAs under frequency-dependent multipath propagation largely unexplored. To address this gap, we investigate a downlink multi-band MA communication system where a common physical MA configuration is shared across multiple communication bands. Such sharing induces an inherent configuration conflict, as different bands often favor substantially divergent MA configurations. We first develop a frequency-dependent multipath channel model with shared propagation geometry but band-dependent multipath component powers and phases. Using this model, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing user-band assignment, MA positioning, and transmit precoding. We further establish a cross-band spatial scaling relationship for the normalized channel power and derive both a position-independent channel gain upper bound and a sum-rate upper bound. Based on these results, we propose a cross-band analysis-guided optimization (CAGO) algorithm and a cross-band graph transformer (CBGT) to reduce online optimization complexity. Numerical results validate the derived cross-band spatial relationship and show that CAGO consistently outperforms the narrowband, wideband, and fixed-antenna benchmarks while remaining close to the idealized independent-MA benchmark. Additionally, CBGT with online refinement achieves near-CAGO sum-rate performance with substantially lower online computational cost, providing a practical framework for exploiting the spatial reconfiguration capability of MAs in multi-band communication systems.
authors: Guangchen Wang; Zhifeng Tang; Haiyao Yu; Nan Yang; Salman Durrani; Xiangyun Zhou

title: Extended Target Imaging in Non-Ideal Distributed ISAC Systems: A Hierarchical Off-Grid Approach
summary: In future integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures offer high-resolution imaging capabilities. However, reconstructing real-world extended targets is physically challenging due to continuous anisotropic surface scattering and complex occlusions, especially in the presence of system synchronization errors. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage computational imaging framework for extended target reconstruction. In Phase I, an incoherent coarse imaging process is performed to serve as a reliable initializer for subsequent high-resolution coherent image generation. By performing line-of-sight (LOS) interference suppression and leveraging network-wide topological constraints, timing and phase offsets are calibrated. This enables image construction by back-projection (BP) and the coarse identification of target contours using the probabilistic Hough transform (PHT). In Phase II, a joint target position and orientation off-grid compensation model is established, capturing Lambertian diffuse and specular reflections on continuous facets via a first-order Taylor expansion. To tackle severe occlusion and spatial grid mismatches, we propose the bilinear off-grid approximate message passing (BiOG-AMP) algorithm. BiOG-AMP iteratively updates surface visibility and dictionary matrices, enforcing physical consistency across distributed transceiver views. Theoretical analysis derives compressed sensing error bounds, Fisher information limits, and linearization error scaling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively eliminates imaging artifacts and exhibits superior robustness against synchronization offsets and grid mismatches compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
authors: Xin Tong; Yu Ge; Alireza Pourafzal; Dario Tagliaferri; Henk Wymeersch

title: A Personalized and Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System for Psychomotor Learning
summary: Intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) have advanced learner motivation and personalization in cognitive domains, but extending these gains to psychomotor tasks remains challenging. Existing psychomotor ITSs rely on learner models built before instruction or updated once per module, leaving open how to use real-time assessments of learner cognitive state for finer-grained personalization. Psychomotor learning involves multiple tutoring objectives, including calibrating self-confidence to performance, calibrating workload per the Yerkes-Dodson Law, and driving skill progression toward higher learning stages. How to balance these objectives for learners, and adjust that balance over time, remains open. This study proposes and evaluates an online personalization algorithm that continuously reprioritizes tutoring objectives to match learners' evolving needs. Rather than weighting objectives equally, the actor-critic-inspired algorithm dynamically updates reward weights using recent measures of self-confidence, workload, and performance. These weights inform a multi-input, multi-output cognitive control framework that synthesizes learner-specific tutoring policies via model-based planning. The approach was evaluated in a human-subject study (N = 40) with a 2D quadrotor landing task. Clustering of the learned reward weights revealed distinct prioritization patterns across learners, indicating the algorithm captures heterogeneity in learner needs. Learners whose weights shifted more substantially tended to reach higher final performance, and those whose weights consistently emphasized workload calibration achieved the strongest outcomes. These findings advance online learner modeling and control-based personalization in psychomotor ITSs, showing how adaptive tutoring can better support learning by aligning instructional decisions with learners' evolving cognitive and performance states.
authors: Madeleine Shuhn-Tsuan Yuh; Neera Jain

title: POMDPs with Lipschitz-Continuous Belief-Dependent Rewards Have Lipschitz-Continuous Value Functions
summary: We establish the vector (or elementwise) Lipschitz continuity of value functions for partially observed Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with reward functions that are Lipschitz-continuous functions of the posterior probability distribution of the state (i.e., the belief). Our results significantly tighten existing Lipschitz results for this class of POMDPs on infinite horizons, with previous results only yielding finite constants for discount factors less than 0.5, while our results yield finite Lipschitz constants for all discount factors less than 1. The significance of our Lipschitz constants is illustrated through their use in heuristic search value iteration (HSVI) to construct (finite) piecewise-linear value function approximations.
authors: Timothy L. Molloy

title: Statistical Design of Multi-BD-RIS-Assisted User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO
summary: We study the uplink of a user-centric (UC) cell-free massive MIMO system assisted by multiple beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs), under imperfect channel state information (CSI) and pilot reuse. The BD-RISs are modeled as reciprocal, lossless, group-connected scattering networks. We first derive the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimation statistics for each user's aggregate channel to its serving access points (APs). To avoid frequent CSI acquisition and RIS reconfiguration, we optimize the BD-RIS scattering matrices using long-term channel statistics, allowing their configurations to remain fixed over multiple coherence blocks. Specifically, we minimize the sum of normalized mean-square errors (NMSEs) of the MMSE aggregate channel estimators, subject to the symmetry and unitarity constraints of the group-connected architecture. We develop a product-manifold Riemannian optimization algorithm and analyze its convergence and computational complexity. To evaluate uplink spectral efficiency (SE), we separately derive a closed-form expression for the effective SINR under maximum ratio (MR) combining at the central processing unit (CPU) and establish a lower bound on the achievable ergodic SE. The SINR derivation accounts for the statistical dependence among channels associated with different APs due to shared BD-RIS-assisted propagation paths, including cross-AP second-order statistics under pilot reuse. Numerical results show that moderate group connectivity retains most of the NMSE improvements achieved by full connectivity, with larger optimization gains as BD-RIS-assisted paths strengthen relative to direct AP-user links. They also reveal that lower estimation NMSE does not necessarily lead to higher uplink SE.
authors: Mohammad Ezaz; Azadeh Vosoughi

title: PMU Foundation Model Bridge: A Tool for Connecting Synchrophasor Streams to Time Series Foundation Models
summary: This paper presents PMU Foundation Model Bridge, an open source tool that connects online phasor measurement unit (PMU) or phasor data concentrator (PDC) streams to publicly available time series foundation models (TSFM). Through a desktop interface or command line interface, users can select measurement channels, define preprocessing, choose TSFMs, and configure outputs. In the initial release, 4 publicly available TSFMs were supported, including Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Timestral, and TimesFM-3. The tool supports both file and synchrophasor streaming outputs, therefore enabling both offline use and integration into C37.118-based online workflow applications. In addition to supporting raw synchrophasor data, the framework provides a preprocessing layer for deriving customized additional quantities for forecasting. The tool is validated using a virtual PMU and real-time laboratory measurements from a frequency disturbance recorder (FDR). The tool aims to support community research on combining synchrophasor technology with TSFMs.
authors: Haozong Wang; Jiahui Yang; Yuru Wu; Chujie Zeng; Qian Liu; Yan Wen; Yayu Yang; Muhammad Umar Afzaal; Yilu Liu

title: A SysML v2 Domain Library for ROS2 Robot Architectures
summary: Systems engineers who model a ROS2 robot in SysML v2 must first model ROS2 itself. Its nodes, communication endpoints, message types, lifecycle states, quality-of-service policies, and coordinate frames have no ready definitions in the language, so each project reconstructs them. We present ros2-sysmlv2, a native SysML v2 domain library that supplies these definitions for reuse. A robot model imports the library and specializes its definitions to declare its own nodes, ports, connections, frames, and parameters. The library maps ROS2 concepts to SysML v2 definitions and usages and organizes them in Primitives, Infrastructure, and Application layers. We check its declarations for parity with the ROS2 Jazzy sources they model. Because every ROS2 element of a model specializes a library definition, a tool can select those elements by type. We state what this selection is and use it for a round trip. A ROS2 package is generated from the selection, and a monitor generated with the package compares the running graph with the same selection and reports every departure against the model. The generation-gap workflow derives topic endpoints and parameter declarations while preserving developer-owned node algorithms. In a case study on a generated ground robot, the generated conformance monitor reported each of the three departures that we introduced in the implementation. The library is distributed as a versioned package that any SysML v2 model can import.
authors: Sai Sandeep Damera; John S. Baras

title: Automated screening of Parkinson's Disease using Smooth Pursuit Eye Movements
summary: Smooth pursuit eye movements are frequently altered in Parkinson's disease, but previous studies have relied mainly on conventional parameters that describe the relationship between gaze and target. This study investigates whether complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of the gaze position sequences can support the automatic screening of Parkinson's disease. Gaze position sequences were recorded with a video eye tracker in 41 participants with early Parkinson's disease and 47 healthy controls during 12 smooth pursuit tasks. Four experimental frameworks and four embedding delay strategies were compared. The selected experimental setting combined baseline wander removal with a fixed embedding delay. After feature selection, a support vector machine was trained for each task and axis and their outputs were combined in a mixture of experts. The pipeline was developed in 70 participants and evaluated on an external test set of 18 participants. On the external test set, the pipeline obtained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86. The most informative features described less persistent and more irregular gaze position sequences in Parkinson's disease, mainly along the horizontal axis. These results support complexity and nonlinear dynamics measures of smooth pursuit as candidate markers for Parkinson's disease screening, pending validation in larger independent cohorts.
authors: J. Camilo Puerta-Acevedo; Maria F. Alcala-Durand; Julián D. Arias-Londoño; Elisa Luque-Buzo; Francisco Grandas-Pérez; Juan I. Godino-Llorente

title: Contract-Based Agentic Systems Engineering: Delegation as Quotient for Assured System Design
summary: A component an agent builds from a prompt can satisfy it and still break the system it joins, because the prompt omits what its neighbours assume of it. The artifact to hand over is computed, not written. A SysML v2 requirement with assumed and required constraints is an assume/guarantee contract, so when a system requirement is decomposed over fixed neighbours, the open component's requirement is the contract quotient, the weakest sound one, and again a SysML v2 requirement. Its required constraints carry the neighbours' assumptions, which a requirement for the mission alone drops and unit tests with mocked neighbours cannot reach. Signal Temporal Logic is closed under the quotient. We build the requirements, with derivation, allocation, satisfaction and verification, as a SysML~v2 model and compute the quotient from it. A case study delegates the local controller of a simulated warehouse robot, whose route crosses a worker's path and ends at a dock, to one language model under the quotient requirement, a mission-only requirement and a natural-language task, and scores the deliveries on live episodes against the system requirement from ground truth.
authors: Sai Sandeep Damera; Ryan Matheu; John S. Baras

title: Graph Spectral Series and Its Signatures
summary: Bandlimitedness is a central modeling assumption in graph signal processing (GSP), but many graph signals exhibit substantial energy throughout the graph-frequency domain. We introduce a new framework for analyzing such non-bandlimited signals by treating their graph Fourier spectra as ordered sequences and representing them with path signatures. Specifically, motivated by the observation that non-bandlimited graph spectra often display rough, time-series like behavior, we introduce the notion of graph spectral series and develop a signature-based representation that captures global spectral structure without frequency truncation. We establish conditions under which the proposed representation is continuous and characterize its information-preserving properties. We further provide an asymptotic interpretation of graph spectral series for sequences of expanding graphs. Experiments on real-world trend-prediction and change-detection tasks show that signature features can improve performance over representations based directly on the original graph signals. The proposed approach provides a novel principled signature-based tool for analyzing non-bandlimited graph signals.
authors: Feng Ji; Jingyang Dai; Apostolos Evangelidis; Xingchao Jian; Marco Rauscher; Alexander Schell

title: Concurrent Space-Based Observer Placement and Scheduling for Cislunar Space Domain Awareness
summary: As interest in cislunar space grows, so does the need for space domain awareness (SDA) capabilities to safely support missions. To enhance cislunar SDA capabilities, the use of space-based observers has been proposed. Prior research has explored optimizing observer placement but has not considered scheduling limitations. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that concurrently optimizes the placement and scheduling of space-based observers for cislunar SDA. Our work considers three aspects of observer scheduling: sensor tasking, communication, and charging. We utilize a scenario-based approach that generalizes observer placement for unknown targets while applying scheduling constraints to each scenario. However, this problem quickly becomes difficult for commercial solvers to handle as the number of scenarios grows. As an alternative, a column generation approach is employed to introduce well-performing schedules into the problem for each orbital slot. A comparative analysis is performed across multiple instances to evaluate the performance of column generation against that of a commercial solver. A case study is then conducted in which the performance of the observers' placement from the concurrent formulation is tested against a set of validation target sets and compared with the performance of two baselines in which placement and scheduling are performed sequentially.
authors: Dominic K. Amato; Hang Woon Lee

title: On the Discernibility of Topology Changes in Networked LTI Systems
summary: This article investigates the discernibility of topology changes in networked linear time-invariant systems, with particular focus on edge disconnection. We introduce a new notion of discernibility motivated by a limitation of the definition commonly adopted in the literature. In consensus networks, topology changes are inherently indiscernible for all initial conditions belonging to the synchronization subspace. To overcome this issue, we first introduce the notion of dynamical discernibility of a topology change for elementary consensus networks. This notion explicitly disregards the intrinsic indiscernibility associated with states in the consensus subspace. We characterize this property for directed communication graphs and then specialize the resulting conditions to topology changes arising from either the disconnection of an edge or a variation in its weight. We then extend the analysis to networks of homogeneous agents by introducing discernibility modulo synchronization, which factors out the unavoidable indiscernibility associated with synchronized trajectories. We derive a general characterization showing how discernibility depends jointly on the topology change and on the dynamics of the individual agents. Finally, we specialize the analysis to undirected communication graphs and show that, under mild additional assumptions, discernibility modulo synchronization is equivalent to the dynamical discernibility of the corresponding topology change. This establishes a direct connection between the two notions and extends existing results on the discernibility of topology variations in dynamical networks. The resulting characterizations are then further specialized to the case of edge disconnection.
authors: Giulio Fattore; Maria Elena Valcher

title: Physical Layer Security in Chirp Permuted AFBM
summary: We propose a physical-layer security scheme for affine filter bank modulation (AFBM), a waveform proposed for sixth-generation (6G) integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). AFBM contains two discrete affine Fourier transforms, one for precoding and one for spreading, and the scheme permutes, with one secret key per transform, the chirp sequence that each transform places between two Fourier stages. A wrong key is then conjugated by a discrete Fourier transform into a dense matrix, the restoration of complex orthogonality fails, and the intrinsic filter-bank interference reaches the detector. Over a doubly-dispersive channel, an eavesdropper with perfect channel state information, co-located with the legitimate receiver and holding either key wrong, keeps a bit error rate near 0.5 and a rate below 0.09 bit/symbol, also under a blind carrier-phase attack. Compared with a single-permutation variant, the double scheme costs about 2 dB of peak-to-average power ratio and enlarges the search space from 10^61 to 10^93.
authors: Pedro Schuves Marodin; Henrique L. Senger; Gustavo P. Gonçalves; Hyeon Seok Rou; Bruno S. Chang; Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu; Didier Le Ruyet

title: Fully-Automated Multi-Modal Registration of Timelapse Zebrafish OCT+LS Images
summary: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and light sheet (LS) fluorescence microscopy provide complementary views of tissue morphology and molecular expression, offering a powerful approach for studying embryonic development. However, longitudinal integration of OCT+LS images is challenging because the modalities differ substantially in contrast, spatial resolution, field of view, and visible anatomical features, while embryo growth and movement introduce additional misalignment over time. These challenges stem from both the scale and multimodal nature of the OCT and LS image stacks. We present a fully automated three-dimensional rigid registration framework for aligning OCT and LS volumes of developing zebrafish embryos acquired from 21 to 48 hours post fertilization (HPF). The method does not require pre-existing segmentations or cross-modal feature correspondences, which are often unreliable because OCT and LS capture fundamentally different tissue properties. Registration performance was evaluated across developmental time points using mean target registration error (mTRE) and compared across multiple similarity metrics and optimization methods. Normalized cross-correlation combined with particle swarm optimization produced the most accurate and consistent registration, achieving the lowest mTRE at every evaluated time point compared with the alternative methods. The registration establishes spatial correspondence between OCT tissue morphology and LS fluorescence signals throughout development, enabling integrated longitudinal analysis of structural and molecular changes in living embryos.
authors: Mahshid Babeli Nia; Leah A. Lewis; Mohammad Mobarak Karim; Manmohan Singh; Arne C. Lekven; Guoning Chen; Kirill V. Larin; David Mayerich

title: Terra-Fi: Decoupling Sensing and Wireless Depths for Sustainable Deep Underground Monitoring
summary: Wireless underground sensor networks (WUSNs) enable in-situ monitoring of subsurface processes and buried assets to deliver substantial social and economic benefits across diverse verticals. However, meter-scale underground monitoring remains challenging since conventional WUSNs place the entire underground device at the target sensing depth, where severe soil-induced attenuation significantly degrades communication reliability and makes wireless energy transfer (WET) inefficient and even impractical. To address this limitation, we propose Terra-Fi, a novel shallow-hub and deep-sensing architecture that decouples the sensing depth from the wireless communication and energy-replenishment depth. In Terra-Fi, a shallow wireless hub is deployed at a depth favorable for communication, WET, and maintenance, while application-specific sensing probes are extended to meter-scale target layers through power-and-signal feeders. On this basis, we first examine the depth limitations of underground communication and WET and compare representative monitoring architectures. Then, we present its system architecture, operation flow, and potential benefits. Through a precision agriculture case study, our numerical results reveal that Terra-Fi establishes more robust wireless connectivity and a longer operational lifetime than conventional fully buried WUSN architectures, particularly at greater sensing depths and higher volumetric water content. Moreover, its performance gain can be enhanced through time allocation and transmission-configuration optimization. Finally, we pinpoint practical challenges and future research directions for deploying Terra-Fi into WUSN systems.
authors: Kaiqiang Lin; Mohamed-Slim Alouini

title: Impact of Synchronization Offsets and CSI Feedback Delays on Coherent Joint Transmission in Distributed MIMO-OFDM
summary: This paper studies the impact of synchronization offsets and CSI feedback delay on coherent joint transmission (CJT) in distributed MIMO-OFDM systems. Unlike conventional co-located MIMO, distributed CJT is highly sensitive to transmitter-dependent synchronization impairments because coherent combining requires phase, frequency, and timing alignment across geographically separated transmitters. Received signal models are derived for residual timing offsets, carrier frequency offsets (CFOs), sampling clock offsets (SCOs), phase noise, and channel variations accumulated during channel state information (CSI) feedback delay. The corresponding spectral efficiency (SE) expressions quantify the degradation in capacity due to loss in coherent-combining gain caused by residual phase rotations, inter-carrier interference (ICI), and precoder misalignment. The SE expressions are numerically evaluated to determine synchronization requirements for maintaining negligible SE degradation, yielding the following findings: a Gaussian-distributed start-time jitter with a standard deviation below 10\% of the sampling period results in negligible SE degradation, with the SE loss decreasing from 0.68\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 0.17\% at 40 dB. A normalized CFO standard deviation of 0.001 also results in negligible ICI-induced degradation, with the SE loss increasing from 0.05\% at an SNR of 0 dB to 2\% at 40 dB. At an SNR of 26 dB, limiting the SE loss to 5\% yields feasible operating points with clock-error standard deviations up to 50 ppb, Doppler-delay products up to 0.1, and phase-tracking error standard deviations up to $40^{\circ}$ at carrier frequency of 3.5 GHz with 30 kHz sub-carrier spacing with 15.36 MHz sampling rate.
authors: Kumar Sai Bondada; Daniel J. Jakubisin; R. Michael Buehrer

title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
summary: Higher-order Ambisonics (HOA) is an attractive format for immersive spatial audio, but its high channel count and directional properties present significant audio coding challenges. The widely deployed Opus audio codec supports HOA through Channel Mapping Families 2 and 3 (RFC 8486), which code and transmit every Ambisonics channel, so the bitrate grows quadratically with the spherical harmonic order. We introduce SEMAC, which instead represents an Ambisonics signal by a quantized full-order directional energy envelope together with fewer CELT-coded transport channels. CELT separates a per-band energy envelope from the signal shape and restores it after quantization, and SEMAC generalizes this principle to directional signals. Since the reduced transport spans only a lower-dimensional subspace, the decoder re-imposes the envelope observed at the encoder input, restoring the directional energy distribution at full order. A MUSHRA test on fifth-order material compares SEMAC against Opus CMF~3 in matched configurations at 512 and 768 kbit/s. SEMAC with 16 of 36 transport channels is rated above full-order CMF~3 at both rates, and at equal transport channel count above order truncation. The proposed SEMAC strategy of coding fewer transport channels with the directional envelope is found perceptually preferable to coding all HOA channels at low precision.
authors: Christoph Hold; Jan Buethe; Jean-Marc Valin; Jan Skoglund; Toni Hirvonen; Nils Peters

title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
summary: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.
authors: Hamza Touati; Raffaele Viterbo; Mattia Brambilla; Sandra Roger; Carmen Botella-Mascarell

title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
summary: Auditory attention decoding (AAD) seeks to identify the attended talker from brief noninvasive brain recordings by comparing neural responses with competing speech streams. Recent electroencephalography (EEG) decoders report nearly perfect accuracy from one second of data, yet we show that this performance fails to generalize to unseen speech because models exploit trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues instead of speech evoked neural activity. We introduce CoupleFlow, which decodes attention through temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings. Its predictions remain at chance when the brain signal contains no informative coupling, preventing shortcuts based on speech content or talker identity. A conditional flow matching head implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information between brain and speech. This rule is Bayes optimal when the recording depends only on the attended talker and removes preferences for speech that is likely a priori. We evaluate CoupleFlow with content disjoint splits recovered from the audio and null tests that distinguish genuine temporal coupling from trial recognition. Across nine EEG and magnetoencephalography (MEG) datasets processed through a common pipeline, spanning four languages, high density EEG recordings, listeners with hearing impairment, and a room with multiple talkers, CoupleFlow outperforms linear and deep baselines while all null tests remain at chance. Finally, we derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts accuracy across window lengths from a single parameter per dataset and predicts that parameter from the strength of neural speech tracking. This law identifies recording signal to noise ratio as a limit on decoding speed and reliability and estimates the window length required to reach a target accuracy.
authors: Ali Alavi; Donald S. Williamson

title: Modeling Liquid-Cooled Data Centers in EnergyPlus
summary: As AI workloads accelerate data center transition toward high-density racks with direct-to-chip (DTC) liquid cooling, existing simulation tools remain limited in evaluating whole-building and multi-year efficiency. To bridge this gap, we develop a native EnergyPlus object, ElectricEquipment:ITE:LiquidCooled, that models DTC liquid cooling for chilled-water and warm-water architectures as plant-loop components. It couples facility-water loops, rack-side secondary loops, coolant distribution units, and chip-junction temperatures within a single solver. Validation against an independent Modelica implementation across 21 operating conditions, including two full-year runs compared at one-minute resolution, yields loop-temperature RMSE at or below 0.021 K, well within the 0.1 K acceptance threshold. Our case study demonstrates that warm-water liquid cooling reduces annual PUE from 1.43 to 1.25, eliminates on-site water use, and cuts total facility energy by 37.9% relative to an air-cooled baseline. By embedding liquid-cooling logic into EnergyPlus, our work provides whole-building, long-term energy modeling for high-density AI infrastructure within an open-source framework.
authors: Yun-Dam Ko; Dipashreya A. Sur; Cade Napier; Carlos D. Díaz-Marín; Rishee K. Jain

title: Classical, Machine Learning, and Hybrid Solvers for Partial Differential Equations: An Evidence-Weighted Review and Decision Framework
summary: Machine learning for partial differential equations raises a practical question: when are classical, learned, or hybrid solvers justified? This survey compares the three families in a decision framework organized by data availability, query volume, and certification needs. An amortization law, tested on parametric Darcy flow, shows that surrogates trained on solver-generated data break even only after many queries, beyond thirty thousand for errors below one percent. An evidence ladder, a benchmark reanalysis, and three case studies show that claims of speedup and generalization carry the weakest evidence. Solver choice should follow regime, query volume, and evidence quality, not method novelty.
authors: Yingchao Huang; Xin Wang; Shanshan Yao; Fanhua Zeng; Wei Peng

title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
summary: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, roughly half of the gain of an idealized reference.
authors: Meizhen Zhuo; Gunter Wolff; Stephan ten Brink; Silvio Mandelli

title: Trust-Region Benders for Scalable Multiperiod Expansion Planning for Transmission and Storage
summary: Transmission expansion planning (TEP) seeks to identify cost-effective investment strategies that enable power systems to reliably meet future demand, while accounting for the location, timing, and operational impacts of infrastructure upgrades. As demand grows and renewable penetration increases, there is growing interest in jointly modeling energy storage investments to enhance operational flexibility. This work presents a multiperiod formulation that co-optimizes transmission reconductoring and energy storage installation across multiple planning periods. To solve the resulting large-scale problem efficiently, a Benders decomposition with per-period trust-region stabilization and a relaxation-based warm-start procedure is proposed. The approach is demonstrated on a 2,000-bus Texas system, producing an investment plan spanning 2030-2045 with optimality gap below 1.0%, and is compared against a rolling-horizon approach to highlight the benefits of multiperiod coordination.
authors: Kevin Wu; Rabab Haider; Pascal Van Hentenryck

title: Density control of large-scale multi-agent systems via tuning of agent interactions
summary: Collective behavior in biological systems emerges through adaptive interactions among units, enabling large populations to coordinate without centralized control. This mechanism raises the question of whether collective behavior in engineered multi-agent systems can likewise be regulated by modifying the interaction law between agents, rather than by directly controlling individual units. To answer this question, we consider large-scale multi-agent systems evolving on a ring and treat the interaction kernel as a time-varying control variable whose evolution regulates the collective dynamics. Using a mean-field formulation, we develop a framework for the analysis and design of kernel-based controllers. We derive explicit conditions for controllability in application-relevant scenarios, and synthesize a state-feedback controller to regulate the kernel dynamics, validated on the microscopic, discrete dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and robustness to unmodeled perturbations. This work constitutes a first step in the design of bio-inspired control strategies for large-scale multi-agent systems by modulation of interactions between agents.
authors: Mena Zkhary; Alain Boldini

title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising
summary: Low-count imaging arises when limited illumination or dose yields only a few detected particles in microscopy, such as photons or electrons, causing measurements to be dominated by signal-dependent Poisson shot noise. Supervised denoisers typically require paired clean and noisy observations, whereas many self-supervised approaches exploit spatial or temporal redundancy without directly estimating the underlying particle-arrival process. We introduce PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework based on particle-arrival-rate matching. By modeling particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process, PARM identifies the conditional particle-arrival-rate field with the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. Poisson thinning then splits each observation into complementary lower-exposure views that provide self-supervised rate targets for one another. In implementation, the network estimates the normalized spatial allocation of the conditional rate, while the observed total count determines its global particle mass. Experiments on synthetic data, natural-video sequences corrupted with Poisson noise, and real low-dose electron microscopy demonstrate leading or competitive performance while effectively preserving fine structures. PARM therefore provides a statistically grounded approach to low-count image denoising when clean references are unavailable.
authors: Huazhen Liu; Zipei Yan; Jizhou Li

title: Cross-Scenario Controller Parameter Transformation from Real-World Driving Data through Flow Matching
summary: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems have become increasingly widespread, aiming to support drivers, reduce workload, and improve traffic safety. However, many systems are rarely used because their behavior feels unnatural and does not match individual driving behavior. The growing availability of large-scale, real-world human driving data enables more human-like and driver-individual assistance functions. This paper formulates the adaptation of Adaptive Cruise Control parameters as a driver-individual scenario-to-scenario transport problem, transforming controller parameters from one driving context to another. Using flow matching, we train a generative model to predict the target-scenario behavior of previously unseen drivers from only a few demonstrations in a source scenario. We compare the approach with a linear parameter-shift baseline and evaluate flow-matching variants incorporating driver-consistent coupling, driver embeddings, and classifier-free guidance based on driving profiles extracted from trajectory data using a variational autoencoder.
authors: Christian Zink; Maik Pfefferkorn; Eric Lenz; Felix Kallmeyer; Rolf Findeisen

title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
summary: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention Transformer (TAGAT) with the LLM through confidence-gated fusion. TAGAT captures structural dependencies among transmission lines, while the LLM extracts representations from early-stage power-flow observations and aggregated cascade descriptors. The frameworks are evaluated on 30,000 simulated cascading failure scenarios for each of the IEEE 118-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems. Using only the first four cascade steps, the hybrid framework achieves weighted F1 scores of 0.94 and 0.92, respectively. In cross-system transfer from IEEE 118-bus to IEEE 300-bus, it achieves 0.72 zero-shot accuracy, improving to 0.83 with limited target-system calibration, outperforming standalone models and conventional baselines. These results show the potential of combining graph-based structural learning with foundation models to improve cascading failure severity prediction and cross-system transferability.
authors: Soumav Biswas; Mia Naeini

title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
summary: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.
authors: Jonas Emrich; Karin Narushima; Lena Wunderl; Philipp Wunderl; Tobias Jensch; Maximilian Huber; Peter Ewert; Peter Fierlinger; Annette Wacker-Gussmann; Reinhard Heckel

title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
summary: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.
authors: Raul C. Sîmpetru; Amin Olamazadeh; Devon Rohlf; Vlad Cnejevici; Alessandro Del Vecchio

title: Iterative Behavioral Identification for Covert Misappropriation Attacks
summary: We present a data-driven, three-phase framework for covert misappropriation attacks on closed-loop networked control systems. A man-in-the-middle (MITM) adversary, with access only to intercepted input-output data, incrementally identifies the plant's behavioral subspace while maintaining stealth under an infinity-norm intrusion-detection system (IDS). Phase 1 collects an initial rank-deficient Hankel matrix using a low-amplitude probing signal that satisfies an analytical stealth bound. Phase 2 adapts online rank-increasing experiment design to the closed-loop setting, using causal predictor-based masking to limit IDS residuals while the Hankel rank grows from 1 to the full behavioral rank n + mL in exactly n + mL - 1 steps. We show that the identified subspaces are strictly nested and that the projection error of any desired trajectory decreases monotonically, strictly so almost surely at each rank increase. Phase 3 employs the final Hankel matrix in a DeePC-style optimization to synthesize a covert attack that tracks an arbitrary reference while respecting the IDS constraint. Simulations on a DC motor with PI control demonstrate full-rank identification and stealthy tracking. Stealth is guaranteed analytically in Phases 1 and 3 and is numerically supported in Phase 2. The method is model-free and assumes noise-free LTI dynamics.
authors: Victor Mattos; Amit Bhaya; Daniel Sadoc Menasche; Alan O. de Sá

title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
summary: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.
authors: Heedong Do; Angel Lozano

title: An Evidence-Guided Framework for Tissue-Barrier Impedance Review: Deletion and Resistance Sensitivity
summary: Reviewing tissue-barrier impedance requires connecting spectral anomalies with resistance estimates and experimental context. We present an evidence-guided framework that coordinates numerical checks and traceable actions for human review. In-house simulations assess the effect of removing flagged frequencies, public datasets test model adaptation, and local measurements demonstrate the review workflow. Removing flagged frequencies reduced resistance error under quadratic objectives, whereas robust fitting showed little average benefit from deletion and a mean error increase for endpoint-pair perturbations. High errors clustered around a few fitted circuit parameter sets, highlighting the value of examining parameter identifiability. Under the tested noise and perturbation conditions, these findings support robust full-spectrum estimation, flag-guided inspection, and matched sensitivity checks.
authors: Leo Yang; Yingtong Zhou

title: Enabling 3GPP-Driven Services Over Optical Transport Network
summary: We demonstrate a multi-layer slicing architecture enabling deployment of 3GPP network slices as self-contained, connected functions atop optical transport slices. The system provides Optical Spectrum as a Service (OSaaS) by integrating disaggregated optical control, multi-tenant orchestration, and telemetry-based optimization via standard interfaces.
authors: Renato Ambrosone; Ramon Casellas; Alessio Giorgetti; Riccardo Schips; Stefano Straullu; Pablo Armingol Robles; Óscar González de Dios; Francisco Javier Moreno; Enrique Fernandez; José Manuel Rivas-Moscoso; Francesco Aquilino; Antonino Nespola; Vittorio Curri

title: Investigating the trackability of landmarks in NBI and WLI
summary: Reliable visual tracking of anatomical landmarks in endoscopic video is a key prerequisite for computer-assisted interventions in laryngeal surgery. While Narrow Band Imaging (NBI) is clinically established for enhancing vascular contrast, its effect on automated tracking relative to conventional White Light Imaging (WLI) remains unexplored. We present a quantitative comparison of landmark trackability in NBI and WLI using a forward-backward error framework applied to 61 endoscopic videos from 39 patients. Two regions of interest are evaluated: the vocal folds (VF) and mucosa with a prominent vascular pattern (MPVP). We compare a classical feature-based tracker (CSRT) against learning-based point trackers (CoTracker3-Online and TrackOnR) across both modalities. NBI consistently reduced the forward-backward error in both regions, reaching statistical significance for the vocal folds, while failure rates stayed low. These findings indicate that NBI can improve tracking robustness in laryngeal endoscopy, with implications for motion analysis, navigation, and robotic assistance.
authors: Jonas Below; Piermarco Gerli; Anna Jötten; Dennis Eggert; Axelle Felicio-Briegel; Veronika Volgger; Christian Betz; Alexander Schlaefer

title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction
summary: This letter poses state estimation (SE) as an in-context tabular prediction (ICTP) problem. The key idea is a tabular arrangement in which historical measurement vectors and corresponding state estimates serve as the context, and a new measurement vector forms the query for which we predict a state vector. We propose to use tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on synthetic data, whose weights are never updated, so power system data is needed only as context. With frozen TFM weights we estimate the state of 14-, 30-, 33-, 70-, and 118-bus transmission and distribution networks, and do so where weighted least squares (WLS) fails or degrades, under low observability and with bad data. ICTP errors are 11 to 57$\times$ below the per-bus average of the context at full metering, and 1.3 to 4.0$\times$ below it with only 5% of measurements available. With measurements at six buses biased by 8$σ$, the ICTP angle error rises 1.8 to 5.0$\times$ over its bias-free value against 2.5 to 12.7$\times$ for WLS with bad-data detection. Without retraining, ICTP has lower voltage error than DSS$^2$ on both of its feeders, and lower than a retrained TAPINE on two of three reconfiguration sets.
authors: Ayushi Jolotia; Parikshit Pareek

title: Spectrally optimized implicit neural representations mitigate acquisition-related image quality trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI
summary: 4D Flow MRI promises opportunities for non-invasive mapping of neurovascular hemodynamics, but its clinical utility faces trade-offs between resolution, acquisition time, and noise. Deep learning-based super-resolution offers a post-scan solution, but supervised approaches require paired or domain-specific data, while patient-specific physics-informed models can be computationally demanding. This creates a need for unsupervised reconstruction models that can adapt to individual acquisitions without paired high-resolution training data, while remaining robust across anatomy, disease severity, and acquisition quality. To address this, we introduce a spectrally tuned implicit neural representation (INR) framework for intracranial 4D Flow MRI, representing the velocity field as a continuous coordinate-based neural field using WIRE activation functions with tunable spectral bias. Data-driven and physics-informed variants were evaluated in nine cerebrovascular cases spanning healthy controls and moderate-to-severe intracranial atherosclerotic disease, using CFD-derived high-resolution reference fields, MR-realistic synthetic low-resolution inputs, and direct fitting to acquired in-vivo data. Cohort-optimal spectral-bias settings generalized across subjects with only small increases in relative error compared with subject-specific optima, reducing the need for case-specific hyperparameter tuning. Physics-informed regularization provided modest additional accuracy but required substantially longer optimization, whereas the data-driven INR achieved near-comparable reconstruction performance within minutes. The framework also remained robust to acquisition-realistic noise and moderate VENC-dependent aliasing. These findings establish spectrally optimized INRs as a flexible unsupervised approach for mitigating acquisition-related trade-offs in intracranial 4D Flow MRI.
authors: Oliver Welin Odeback; Nerea González-Aranceta; Sebastián Jofre; Javier Bisbal; Edward Ferdian; Alistair A. Young; Pia Callmer; Sameer A. Ansari; Mia Bonini; David Nordsletten; Patrick Winter; Susanne Schnell; Tobias Granberg; Alexander Fyrdahl; David Marlevi

title: Solid State Transformer - Next Generation MV Interface for Native DC loads
summary: About PowerNexa PowerNexa is the project name for a start- up initiative driven by Marco Liserre and Steffan Hansen with the ambition to develop the next generation power grid interface. Battery integration and DC loads Ongoing electrification is fundamentally changing how electrical energy is produced and consumed. DC loads are becoming an integral part of the infrastructure while battery integration is increasingly needed to manage peak demand and address grid capacity constraints. The next generation grid interface PowerNexa aims to combine a fully controllable Medium Voltage grid interface with native battery integration and multiple DC voltage levels, based on an architecture designed for high efficiency, modularity and redundancy.
authors: Steffan Hansen; Marco Liserre; Mohamed Moharram

title: Do LLM-derived text features improve electricity price forecasts beyond document activity? Evidence from Australia's National Electricity Market
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can turn market notices and news into features for electricity price forecasting. Such features also record when documents arrive and whether their extraction failed, so a gain measured against a model without text can reflect document activity as well as content. We add the counts of the same documents and of their failed extractions to a no-text LightGBM model and measure each LLM representation against this activity reference, which needs no additional LLM requests. With gpt-6-luna as the extractor, we forecast Australian electricity prices from operator notices (5-30 minutes ahead) and WattClarity news (day-ahead) after the extractor's documented knowledge cutoff, averaging forecasts over three training seeds. For news, the counts alone lower mean absolute error (MAE) by 3.0%, most of the 3.6% reduction that the better LLM representation achieves relative to the no-text model; its increment beyond the counts is not significant. For notices, two of the three LLM representations lower MAE beyond the counts, by 0.14-0.21% and 0.45-0.52%, whether the counts are cumulative or cover recent windows, whereas the third shows no significant reduction. Time-shifted placebos give mixed evidence on whether these gains require text aligned with the target. Benchmarks using the operator's pre-dispatch forecasts (notices) or price history alone (news) are more accurate than all these text models. Gains against the no-text model and the activity reference differ in sign at individual seeds and, for notices with cumulative counts, in seed-averaged forecasts. Text gains should be reported against both references.
authors: Fanxing Ning; Jianguo Zhu

title: A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections
summary: We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. The proposed approach models multirate systems as impulsive systems with multiple independent jump maps and corresponding jump-time sequences. We tackle analysis and design problems with stability, dissipativity, and robustness objectives, relying on a multi-clock-dependent Lyapunov function parameterization. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.
authors: Julian Berberich

title: Type-based Over-the-Air Computation
summary: Over-the-air computation (OAC) exploits the superposition property of wireless channels to compute functions of distributed data, reducing the communication overhead associated with its multiple access. However, existing OAC frameworks are often designed around specific classes of functions, limiting their applicability to more general nonlinear computations. This paper investigates type-based multiple access (TBMA) as a general framework for OAC, enabling the receiver to recover a histogram of the distributed observations and compute a broad class of functions without modifying the underlying communication scheme. We formulate TBMA as a histogram estimation problem and propose two digital detectors. We prove that a low-complexity successive cancellation algorithm achieves the optimal maximum-likelihood (ML) performance. We derive analytical expressions for the mean squared error (MSE) and compare TBMA with conventional schemes in terms of computation accuracy, transmission duration, bandwidth and energy consumption. Numerical experiments validate the analytical results and demonstrate that, unlike existing OAC techniques, TBMA exhibits an exponential MSE decay with increasing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and constant transmit energy, independently of the function being computed. These findings position TBMA as a step toward more versatile OAC architectures, compatible with existing transmission schemes, and broadening the range of functions that can be computed directly over the wireless channel and enabling new possibilities for distributed computation and decision-making.
authors: Marc Martinez-Gost; Ana Pérez-Neira

title: Regret-Based Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control under Uncertain Traffic States
summary: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.
authors: Chaopeng Tan; Qiongdan Hu; Meng Wang

title: Decision Timescales in Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control: Theory, Methodology, and Validation
summary: Max-pressure (MP) control adapts signal phases to prevailing traffic states, but its decision timescale is typically fixed a priori. This paper treats the decision timescale as an explicit dimension of MP control. We first characterize the trade-off between responsiveness and switching efficiency by quantifying how an equivalent switching loss reduces service capacity over a finite decision interval. This yields a load-dependent critical timescale determined by switching loss and normalized traffic load, together with a performance-oriented operating range above the stability boundary. Building on this result, we propose Variable-Timescale Max-Pressure (VT-MP), in which each intersection selects its decision interval according to local operating conditions, allowing the control timescale to vary across time and space. We establish strong stability of the resulting asynchronous heterogeneous controller under uniformly admissible local loads and bounded decision intervals, and introduce a downstream receiving-supply correction for finite-storage implementation. Three experiments provide mechanism validation and network-level evaluation. A single-intersection experiment confirms that the preferred decision interval increases systematically with traffic load and follows the derived characteristic timescales. In a store-and-forward network, heterogeneous VT-MP reduces total queueing time by 31.0% relative to the best fixed-interval benchmark. In a microscopic 5x5 SUMO network, it reduces mean trip delay by 24.3%, from 213.3 s to 161.5 s, and peak network accumulation by 12.3%. These findings show that the MP decision timescale should be treated as a traffic-state-dependent control variable rather than a fixed implementation parameter.
authors: Chaopeng Tan

title: Heterogeneous Space Data Centers: A Key Paradigm for Future Non-Terrestrial and In-Orbit Services
summary: Lower space-launch cost and advances in AI are driving space-based data centers (SDCs) that provide AI-centric computing and communication services to in-orbit and non-terrestrial assets. However, architectural principles, service models, and energy provisioning for such SDCs, particularly in low-Earth orbit (LEO), remain largely unexplored. We introduce heterogeneous SDCs composed of large and small nodes, differentiated by computing capability, size, and power budget, to support applications spanning ground, aerial, and in-orbit users. We define use cases, node sizing and placement strategies, and interconnection topologies integrating space-to-space and space-to-ground links. Focusing on dawn-dusk LEO configurations, we analyze solar power availability, visibility windows, and latency-aware coverage. Using baseline workloads for typical scenarios, we evaluate latency and service reliability. We quantify energy requirements of different SDC roles and deployment scales, highlighting trade-offs among node size, orbit selection, and service portfolio, and provide design guidance and future research directions for AI infrastructure in space.
authors: Peng Hu; Mustafa Alhassan; Amjad Iqbal

title: Quadrotor Guidance for Tasks along Elliptical Boundary
summary: This paper presents a guidance method that enables a quadrotor uncrewed aerial vehicle to perform inspection tasks along an elliptical boundary enclosing a structure of interest. The proposed guidance approach leverages a bifurcation theory-based framework that supports multiple inspection tasks, including convergence to a desired viewpoint, switching between viewpoints along the boundary, constant-speed elliptical circumnavigation, and circumnavigation with sectorial dwell-time constraint. Stability analysis of the proposed guidance dynamics establishes convergence of the generated reference trajectories to the desired behavior. The control parameters in the proposed method further allow the settling time of the reference trajectory to be specified for each task. The resulting reference velocity expressions are closed-form and algebraically simple, facilitating practical implementation. A qualitative comparison with existing guidance methods highlights the flexibility of the proposed approach in achieving different inspection tasks through a unified framework, while relying on simpler guidance computations. The proposed guidance method is validated through numerical simulations using a six-degree-of-freedom quadrotor model with model uncertainties, and a cascaded sliding-mode controller that tracks the generated reference trajectories under bounded disturbances.
authors: Ravi Khandelwal; Ashwini Ratnoo

title: Melody Guidance for Audio Diffusion Models Without Retraining
summary: Controlling melody in audio generation normally requires training a conditional generative model on audio paired with pitch curves or MIDI notes. We instead guide an existing unconditional diffusion model, originally trained without melody inputs, to follow a target melody without retraining or modifying it. During inference, a differentiable pitch detector steers the sampled audio toward the desired pitches, while the diffusion model keeps it close to the distribution of realistic audio learned during training. Our main contribution is a sampling method that balances these two directions, providing melody control while preserving audio quality. To improve stability, we initialize sampling with a simple synthesized version of the target melody rather than pure noise. Experiments on piano, guitar, and singing voice show melody accuracy comparable to conditional models trained specifically for melody control. Our method therefore adds melody control to existing audio diffusion models without requiring paired melody data or task-specific retraining.
authors: Cristobal Andrade; Sebastian J. Schlecht; Ben Maman; Meinard Müller

title: IAR: An Interaction-Aware Approach to Post-Seek Recovery in Adaptive HLS Streaming
summary: After an unbuffered seek, an adaptive bitrate (ABR) player has little forward buffer at the new position, while its controller may retain a bandwidth estimate from earlier downloads. An expensive first request can delay resumption; later requests may interrupt playback while the buffer rebuilds. We introduce Interaction-Aware Recovery (IAR), a temporary layer around the hls.js ABR controller. After an unbuffered seek, IAR discounts the inherited estimate (γ=0.15) to set a representation ceiling. Normal adaptation continues below it until 8 s of forward buffer has been rebuilt. In a 200-run paired study spanning four network profiles, ten seek positions, and five strategies, a conservative first request reduced resume delay by a paired median of 2.008 s relative to standard hls.js. Keeping a low ceiling through recovery reduced later interruption under stronger degradation but lowered early presented bitrate. IAR and Fixed-Low-Recovery both used L0 in this campaign, so the results did not show an additional benefit from deriving the ceiling from inherited bandwidth. In 60 additional runs under a fixed Moderate profile, we reset the estimator to six controlled scalar priors. IAR's ceiling changed from L0 to L1 and L2 at the predicted thresholds. Resume and recovery times increased at those transitions; presented bitrate varied non-monotonically and was highest at L2. No stalls occurred. These reset-created priors do not reproduce complete, naturally evolved exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) histories. The results show the benefits and presented-quality costs of conservative post-seek recovery, without establishing an advantage for a history-derived ceiling over a fixed low ceiling.
authors: Mahdi Naseri Majd; Amirfarhad Farhadi

title: ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Challenge
summary: This paper presents the ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Grand Challenge, the first community challenge dedicated to benchmarking speech enhancement from millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar vibrometry. The challenge targets realistic through-glass sensing scenarios where microphones are ineffective or impractical.
